2019won5co.author: Karl Schaefer
2019won5co.description:
Description: Daughters Death Star variant.

Update of the classic Matthew Morgan Death Star with newer Anarch cards and a
switch to Daughters of Cacophony. I played an earlier version of this deck last
Week of Nightmares and squeaked into a final with it, but the deck was not
nearly resilient enough. Darby Keeney suggested adding more Conductors and the
sect change for Embraces allowed me to ditch Seattle Committee and Twilight
Camp for better Masters.

In Round 1, I was sandwiched in between Alex and Mark. I had a brief window
where Alex was a 10 pool and I drew my first Revolutionary Council. With Alex's
prey at 1 pool, I had to go for the vote. Mark was showing sporadic intercept
and managed to catch me. My game went downhill quickly as they teamed-up to
bounce Alonso Petrodon to me.

Round 2 was much better, but a slow game with 3 vote decks, so there was lots
of talking. My prey had a Legendary, Cardinal-Benedicted Isouda get
decapitated, so I was mostly in a good position, but with very little card
movement, I was mostly a horde-bleed deck. First Tradition hit the table and
locked quite a few Methuselahs. I was able to work successfully because I had
an un-Converted Yseult, calling my prey's Black Forest Base vote. The game
somewhat devolved from there and I ended with 4vp.

Alex Romano (Group 4/5 Nos Royalty) ->
Mark Loughman (Emerald Legionnaire) ->
Kelly Schultz (The unnamed w/Maleficia) ->
Me ->
Ben Peal (Black Hand toolbox)

I chose to sit as Kelly's prey not remembering what he was playing. The good
thing about The unnamed was that it took him several turns to get it in play. I
had a good opening crypt draw and got Yseult and Angela Preston early. The
Embraces came up quickly.

Mark got Erlik and Erebus, a few Legionnaires and some guns, but spent way too
much. Alex scored an early VP. I never blocked The unnamed and fortunately it
never got the Enkil Cog. I tried to keep my pool total high enough via Con Boon
and for the most part was in good shape. I called my first Revolutionary
Council vote for 14, all pool damage to my prey. Then, using Firebrand unlocked
and call two Con Boons. Unfortunately each ended via Evil Eye, resulting in no
pool gain.

On my next turn, I started with 4 pool. Losing 1 to Contagion and paying 1 more
pool to recycle Revolutionary Council via Garibaldi-Meucci Museum, leaving me
at 2 pool. Ben was at 7 and the vote should have been easy to pass with
Conductor, 2 Barons, 3 Firebrands, and Bastielle Opera House (22 votes), but I
stupidly put The Coven in play on my previous turn, which meant that Kelly's
Horde with Malificia gained blood without having to lock.

I stymied my own oust, as the Horde Evil-Eyed the vote. I spent the next few
actions trying to cycle into some kind of oust, including running Angela
through several different Baron titles, bleeding, calling other votes, but my
math always came up 1 pool short. So, I looked backwards and Kelly was within
range of the the Dominate. A quick deal with Alex was hatched and I called a
Lily Prelude at inferior putting all 4 points on my predator.

Ben gets up to 10 pool and then Alex lunges. He hits Unleash Hell's Fury first,
but manages to finish him off with the other two vampires. I'm sure if another
action were available to him, I would have been off the table as well. Instead,
I start my turn with 2 pool, paying 1 to recur Revolutionary Council again and
call it to oust Ben. I send an Embrace over to burn the vampire in torpor, but
instead burn Warsaw Station. I send a bleed of 1 over to grab the Edge.

Alex plays another Station (his pool is around 20 at this point). He sends in a
bleed with Alonso Petrodon, boosting it to 5 and gets Archoned. He takes a
couple of tool up actions, including Heroic Might. After rushing one of my
Barons into torpor, he passes the turn back to me. Edge pays to grab the
Revolutionary Council again and I easily pass it, leaving Alex at 6 or 7 pool.

Alex plays Pentex on my remaining Baron (Angela) and rushes my only other
"real" Daughter. She survives via Majesty and he attempts to leave defenders.
Alex told me after that he was cycling, looking for a Sudden as he expected me
to play Pentex. I start my turn with 4 pool and all of my remaining cards in my
hand. I play Pentex and there's no Sudden, so we're contesting. I call my other
Revolutionary Council vote, hitting 3 stealth as I bypass his standing vampire.
I had the Daring the Dawn in hand at this point, but in case something went
wrong I wanted her out-of-torpor. The last vote succeeds and I take the table
3-2.
2019won5co.name: (Death) Stars of the Stage

2019won3co.author: Karl Schaefer
2019won3co.description:
Description: Night Moves + Propaganda.

I played this online several times and liked the basic concept. Big thanks to Ke
for helping tune this deck. It worked beautifully today until the finals. Round 1
finshed in 37:30 with a sweep at a four-player table. Round 2 gave me an additional
VP, which tied me for second-place. Both rounds were helped immensely by a first
turn Information Highway. As usual, I lost the die roll, so I was third seed going
into the finals.

Seating:
Me ->
Conner Bell (Legacy of Pander) ->
Mark Loughman (KS Stealth Bleed) ->
John Pattie (Tremere with Potence toolbox) ->
Alex Romano (Henry Taylor Twister)

I ended up exactly where I wanted. I knew if Alex could get set up that none of the
decks at the table would be able to oust him. So, I was hoping to let Mark get John
off the table and out-race the eventual Smiling Jack to get 2vp and win on seeding.

My opening crypt draw was awful, containing no Anarch Converts. I had to dig twice
just to find the first one. So, there was a lot of early discarding of unplayable
cards. Fortunately, the Legacy deck never got one into play, which would have made
my victory impossible. Mark made somewhat quick work of John. In the four-player,
Alex allowed me to call two Diversity, which gave me 12 pool and Alex 8, with Mark
and Conner only gaining 2 pool each. I think it was a mistake for Alex to allow these
votes to go through.

The rest of the game was me crashing into Conner's vampires sometimes with stealth,
sometimes slap fighting. Eventually I oust Conner and continue against Mark in the
same way. Alex tried to deal with Mark to oust me and go heads up, but Alex was
already set up. Mark kept trying to make forward progress, even getting Alex to 3 pool.
Eventually, I got Mark next and conceded my VP to Alex, since I had no way of getting by
Henry Taylor.

I won on seeding in a 2-2-1 result.
2019won3co.name: Propaganda Moves

2019won1co.author: Bill Troxel
2019won1co.description:
Most proud of this deck for the synergy between Mina, Thomasso,
Jake Washington, Shambler rush and Tye Cooper. Mina gets blood
when Tye eats vamps that the Shamblers torporize. She can push
blood to Thomasso with his special. If you push Mina's last
blood to him, you can pop Jake for her in the same phase.

This deck swarms fairly quickly with Shamblers and Legionnaires.
Called "Hybrid" because it uses burn-option cards in addition to
Specialization/Liquidation for dumping cards to power Legionnaires.
If I were to play it again, I might remove the Specializations in
exchange for a couple more Liquidations and a few Funeral Wakes.
That said, Specialization did save me from being ousted by Fame
in torpor in the final round, so it's hard to hate it.
2019won1co.name: Hybrid Legionnaire 4.2

cautiously and trying not to do too much in early game is the secret to this
archetype.

Very minor changes to previous versions. It seems to be particularly important
for this deck to be as slim as possible, so I try to always keep it at 65

2019pnpspb.author: Delmar Sittoni
2019pnpspb.description:
Description: Samedi Trap + reanimated corpse
A very agressive deck, with a combination of rush and bleed 2 with zumbies.

Last table: Me > Maurão's multi rush Lorrie > Henrique's typhonic beast rush > Fabi's Goratrix Wall > Desso's low cap AUS.
A very very long game, with me beeing the bad guy. I got 2vp before my deck finished and somehow survived the rest of
the game (Fabi would get the table in the long run).

Goodies: Comparing with bleed actions, the reanimated corpse does the same damage per action, with the
same blood cost, and less cards (bleed + Govern + Conditioning = 6 pool dmg, costing 2 blood; the zumbies
do the same pool damage for the same cost and only 1 card). Because you spend a lot less slots to do the pool dmg,
you can use them in the form of combat cards that both zumbies and samedies can use, making this deck much harder
to deal with rush and intercept.

Badies: 1- No bleed Deflection! Must have Baroque to rush your predator if he/she is S&B; 2- S&B decks only need
to deal 15 or less damage to oust your first prey, before geting your first VP it is very possible that the entire table is
working against you and everybody can rescue vampires in torpor.

Changes: My deck ended in most my games, so more cards. The 8 and 9 cap vamps only slowed me down, so more of the
low cap ones. A version with anarch convert and revolt could be tested.

Enkidu got himself to regent and did random rush to my poor Charles Delmare, one Entombment and diableri later Charles was the Regent. Final was weird game.

2019hgpp.author: Karl Schaefer
2019hgpp.description:
Description: Grinder-style Emerald Legionnaire deck

When building this deck, I wanted to take the traditional Ventrue/!Ventrue grinder, replace the
Ventrue/!Ventrue with Harbingers and the Dominate with Emerald Legionnaires. There's not an even
math in that conversion, however. There's no good answer to Deflection, since all of the Auspex
bounce locks your vampires. Weighted Walking Sticks don't provide enough permanence nor enough
safety for your vampires lacking Fortitude. Furthermore, space has to be made for Spectral
Divination and Breath of Thanatos for their versatility. While I like the result, in the end, this
is probably just a fightier version of Martin Weinmayer's Emerald Dream.

I wasn't sure what people would play today, but I wanted good defense. I finished up the deck about
2 hours before the event, and found the right mix for today. The final had two fast bleed decks
that I knew about and two decks that I hadn't seen all day.

John M. (Toreador/!Toreador Anarch Toolbox) 0vp ->
John E. (Dem Breed with Madman's Quill) 0vp ->
Me 4vp ->
Mark (Nocturn Bleed) 0vp ->
Will (+Bleeders with AUS/OBF) 1vp

I knew both Mark and Will were strong bleeders, having survived as prey to each deck, I didn't want
to risk that again. I was unsure of the other decks, so decided to be Mark's predator because I
hoped to be able to wear him down during his undirected Nocturn recruitments. I felt that was still
a risky choice. I don't have a lot of Eagle's Sight, so it was possible that Mark could have taken
3vp before I could get him under control.

Going third was perfect for me and I had a great crypt with four different vampires. I got Erebus
in play on turn 2 and on the next turn gave him a Guardian Angel and a Bowl of Convergence. I got
Maldavis in play next. Mark was only taking forward actions early and Will's Cornelius Ottavio had
standing 3 bleed vs. every deck on the table. My predator hit Erebus with a Pentex Subversion,
played Sibyl's Tongue to find a Conceal and immediately tried to burn the Bowl. Maldavis was barely
able to block it. Maldavis took an action to remove the Pentex and drew a block. Mark was going
forward very effectively and I had little to say about it. Will was trying to outrace his predator.
John M, my grand-predator, took two actions to remove the Pentex (Change of Target on the first),
then sunk a big bleed on John E. Erebus was able to block again and tried to do so with almost
every action my predator took. After a few feints, John E got a Creation Rites in play. At this
point, I got my first Legionnaire and then brought out Zygodat. Then knocked off the Creation Rites
with Scourge of the Enochians. Mark started to take undirected actions, as the Nocturns came up. I
wore down his vampires' blood totals (Obtenebration is expensive), but he made really good
progress. When it came to my turn again, I played another Legionnaire normally and mostly held off.
The pool totals are very low for both Will and John M. When a bleed of three gets bounced to me, I
decided that sending it to John M instead of my prey is the better long term move. If Will can get
a VP and I'm the last man standing, I'd win on seeding (or better). John M blocked, but that took
critical resources. On my turn, I Pentexed Mark's fourth vampire and sent my Legionnaires after The
Path of Night. Mark needs to take a lot of Nocturn actions and I lock every minion to keep Mark
from going forward. Will survives and is able to oust John M. John E hits me with a bleed that I
can't block, but doesn't have enough to really hurt me. I ousted Mark with Legionnaires and the
next turn got Will. John E's bloat machine was working well, but his minions were low on blood. I
had The Unmasking and four vampires and three Legionnaires. When I dropped Smiling Jack, John E
conceded with ~30 minutes left in the final.

The critical play, in my mind, was recognizing that I needed to throw John M off the island and let
Will have a VP and the extra pool that comes with it.
2019hgpp.name: Lions and Tigers and Legionnaires, Oh My!

2018fncef0.description:
With Martin's and Bram's success with the Black Jack deck, I wanted to build my own (post-Anthelios) Girls deck to try out the archetype. The way I see it, with Anthelios gone, you'll probably want more than the traditional 9 Ashurs to ensure that you won't be milling your last set. But with too many Ashurs you'll never get to the point where you can really alter your deck composition in a meaningful way with your recursion. So my answer was to go up in Liquidations. The pool gain is also helpful especially considering the nerfing of Villein.
I ended up trying out several silver bullet kind of cards that I knew would be only marginally useful, but with the idea being to mill them to the ash heap and only bring them back if needed, I thought the opportunity cost was pretty low. None of them were really critical and if I play the deck again I'll probably try to cut the deck size down to 80-ish.

Description: Anarch Khazar's Diary Deck

Updated from my Origins version, where I missed the finals on tournament points. I added more
cards, dropping most of my stealth for Liquadation and Sudario Refraction. The minimal stealth
worked well today, but the key to both rounds that the deck performed well in was to get a
Khazar's into play before my predator or prey had any minions to block with.

As I expected it was an ally heavy day with the final having 3 ally decks:
Alex (Garou) 1.5vp ->
Mariya (Anneke/Anson toolbox) 0vp ->
Me 1.5vp ->
Mark (Shamblers and Hookers) 0vp ->
Jeff (Gargoyle Razor Bat wall) 0.5vp

I actually didn't play The Unmasking in the final because of Mark's allies, though he played it a
turn later. Alex had the first oust, but the Diary was primed by that point. I kept whittling Mark
down to 1 pool and putting more wraiths into play, hoping to lunge and get both Mark and Jeff in a
single turn. As time wound down, I got Mark, but on 5 actions I couldn't get a single wraith bleed
to succeed against Jeff. Realizing the with little time remaining my best bet was to turtle up as
both my predator and prey ganged up on me and I could do very little against 4 minions with
standing intercept. I could have probably lasted only a few more turns, but timed was called.

Thanks to Orpheus for a few tips on the deck.

For certain decks I've upped my Converts from 5/13 to 6/13; proved useful for this deck.

2018rasrf0.author: Antti Penttilä
2018rasrf0.description:
As already discused in Deck clinic. Alafin is what makes the deck go.
The ability has to be used to it's fullest, so don't give out free discards to others when they need them. You have to be smart about it...
You will be milling yourself so much that you don't get to play every card in the deck.
But you will be able to use the right cards at the right time, so don't get distracted with things that are "good".
Focus on the cards that will actually win you the game.
Also plan ahead, you have enough recursion to get the things you need, but most of the time you need a turn or 2 to get there, so plan your actions correctly and don't get caught on the critical one.
Overly simplified: If you are thinking: Should I discard to Alafin? The answer is yes... it will get you more Legionnaires and you can get everything back if you really need it...

2018won3co.author: Darby Keeney
2018won3co.description:
Description: Based entirely around abusing Baba Yaga's untap special. Suffers from the star-syndrome, and is completely Pentex-sensitive.

This is way, way thicker a master package than I like to run, but at least 7 are trifles and I expect 5-6 to be clear discards or Heart fodder. But the acceleration is pretty important in getting the deck to function quickly enough to be a factor in the mid-game.
-- I've gone back and forth on Monastery of Shadows in this deck. I've omitted it for now, simply because of the 3-pool cost. The deck could also run a Smiling Jack, but I loathe the way that card makes me play when it's in front of me (or for that matter, anywhere else.)
-- I pulled a Bleeding the Vine for Wash just before heading to Origins. It usually sat in my hand because Pentex exists. Jake Washington was also a late addition, not useful in these 3 games, but low blood totals tend to hamstring this deck.

I thought there was a Flak Jacket in here, but it must have gotten culled for additional transient prevention and untaps.

The bleed retainers are the source of the real offense in the deck, adding to the 3 minions with +1 bleed. At least once per game, Baba Yaga will fire off an Archon-able bleed without any coverage from the Owl Companion. I just press the big red button and hope for the best.

Yes, I know the bounce package is pathetically weak. But Baba Yaga seems to prefer blocking. So I've focused instead on reactions that give both intercept and true untap. Baba Yaga standing tall with 1-3 intercept and 4-5 strength seems to be a significant deterrent to continuing actions.
2018won3co.name: Pictures at an Exhibition

2018won2co.author: Darby Keeney
2018won2co.description:
Description: Starts slowly with some Anarch Revolt pressure and bleeds of 1-2, ramps output with permanents and increasingly dense combat in the late game (Ashur Tablet cycles).

Nana and/or Aksinya tend to drive defense and make opportunistic offensive moves. Smaller minions do most bleeding/rushing in the midgame.

-- Omitting Carlton Van Wyk was a grave error, rectified during this write-up.

Only expected to need 1-2 cycles of Tablets and I was concerned that 2 more would interrupt card flow early in the game. I couldn't go with more acceleration for the same reason, It's also necessary to jettison Masters early in most games, even at "only" 34 cards.
-- The pair of untap locations are mostly used if Aksinya shows in the opening crypt.

Unfortunately, this deck is almost exclusively 1 action per minion per turn with a light reaction package, I had to lean away from a loads of permacept. The Sport Bike above replaces one Raven Spy, because it can be moved and it leverages that tiny bit of untap following equip actions.

Red Question proved to be great. Nana converted mid-action and dropped Monkey Wrench on a Codex bleed in the final. It can also be played after combat on a blocked action, so it's easy to crank out a safety net for the Revolts. Clears the hand easily (burn option or Powerbase:LA) if not needed.

I'm pretty casual about blocking unless permacept AND an untap location come up early. Backrushing remains a control option if the defense angle isn't enough.
2018won2co.name: A Question of When

2018won1co.author: Alex Romano
2018won1co.description:
This deck was built around a conversation I saw on a group about how cardinal
benediction is an inferior card. I just felt that was asinine so I combined it
with some of the most heinous cards in the game to create this little
monstrosity. Fear of Mekhet, Pentex, Banishment, Conceal, Scalpel Tongue,
Disarming Presence and Derange can all be game breaking cards at the right
time. The deck is at its best with an aggressive prey as it can just play the
unassuming role and be at 20+ pool before doing anything of note.

The final was definitely this case as I had a Lasombra stealh bleed prey and a
Mambo Jeanne beat face cross table to scare everyone. I was able to get a
reverse win with my predator going first then his predator and so on. By time
the stealth bleed prey got his VP I was sitting comfortably at around 40 pool
after turns of black forest and capping with Armin's special.

The recursion from Waste Management Operation is essential as there aren't a ton
of offensive votes in the deck. Once in play it needs to be used every turn to
push offensive votes and the right modifiers back into your deck. Protected
resources slows the game down and often times discourages your prey from
attempting to bleed.

Gurchon Hall doesn't need to be in the deck as I never got any mileage out of it.
Probably better off being another Minion Tap or offensive vote. Probably Ancilla
Empowerment with the current Ally heavy climate.
2018won1co.name: Cardinal BeneDICKtion

2018pbuybc.author: Mark Jasper
2018pbuybc.description:
Thanks to Martin Schumacker for playing a similar deck a couple of times on
Lackey and giving me the inspiration to make this deck. The core idea from
Martin is to use Coroner's Contact to pull out whatever Samedi (4 in deck) are
left in the crypt and use Soul Gem with 100% chance of drawing another
Capuchin. You give the Capuchin Obfuscate, the Soul Gem, and Villein down to 2.
Then do the classic Force of Will bleed with Daring the Dawn at inferior and
Conditioning to bleed for 7, unblockable by vampires, burn the Capuchin and get
a new unlocked Capuchin to Villein later. This deck can bloat a ton! Use Under
My Skin (on two actions each) to stealth past allies. Obviously, rushing
allies like Ossian and Garous are really bad news for this deck since Samedi
besides Baroque (Auspex!) have no intercept. The Capuchin is the star, so if
he goes to torpor you're toast. Best strategy is to be patient, wait until all
Samedi are in uncontrolled region, blocking some actions with the Capuchin when
you have Obedience and bouncing bleeds while looking innocent and staying good
on pool. Then, when you're prey gets down to 10 pool or so, Villein down to 3,
Magic out the Soul Gem, and have two left to pay for Force of Will and
Conditioning, get a new Capuchin and repeat, semi-turbo style. Fun deck to
play.
1.5vp in final (won tiebreaker as 2nd seed).
2018pbuybc.name: Semi-Turbo Capuchin

2017pbuhfbc.description: Description: Use Malgorzata's special to get the Capuchin out, then Lord Tremere, wall up and make them obey. Use Magics to get the Capuchin the Erebus Mask, get somebody the Bowl of Convergence or Signet of King Saul if you need it and Heart of Nizchetus if not. Get a Sniper Rifle if there are big caps out there (since they don't obey). Block and bounce carefully. Act recklessly only if you have Mirror Walk in hand. Bloat as needed, tool up, and bleed/vote your prey to death. Allies are bad (they don't obey either), but there are two Far Mastery's, at least, and you have a 9 card hand (or more when you have a Dreams or the Monastery). Lord Tremere gives Mal an extra action and so do Rutor's Hands. Dedicated rush combat is obviously your biggest threat (though the Obediences stop that too as long as they are in your hand and it isn't Enkidu or another 11-cap rusher). I actually had a multi-rush Lazverinus, Thrall of Lambach, deck as my predator in the first round, but he was so busy rushing his stealth bleed predator and grand predator (after his predator was ousted), that he never had a chance to rush me. I actually bled out my prey (when it was down to the two of us) one second before the game timed out. Fun times.

2017rfehf0.author: Petrus Makkonen
2017rfehf0.description:
Took 3GW+10vp in preliminary rounds in Ropecon EQC 2017, Finland Helsinki. Won finals with time as top seed, 0.5VP.

The Finnish title for every iteration is just 'Guido Kuolematon', no matter what's in there. Always remember to add one Guido in there to make it a Guido deck. The rest is pretty much irrelevant.

In here I was initially thinking of ways to deal with Weenie Animalism. Beast is pretty much a free minion for you when Governed down, and deals with 3 blood animalismers with a single Slam!. Put the guys in the freezer to keep up with the blood race.

Rest of the time? Remember all those times when the cross table Obfuscate voter goes to 1 blood with bloody everything after rescues, no one plays interaction and they win the game the next turn? They're not playing a single combat card. Neither does Beast have to.

For extra fun times Beast is always the one who drains Pentexes. You don't really have to worry about that. As long as it's not Angelica or Gratiano you're good to go. It's not that the deck suffers if you're not playing Beast. And you can always beg for removals from cross table... Anyways, you'll get to dodge Pentex with your REAL vampires (coughguidocough) and bleed with Govern.

The crypt around Beast could be whatever. 6 Slams and Beast is all you need. Just don't think you'll have to commit a game plan on him. Don't. This could just as well be Euro Brujah. Or Arika turbo. Or Huitzi MMPA.

Put the deck together in an evening and changed a lot of cards on a whim 15 minutes before the tournament. Should use more Obfuscate and there's some room for weird tinkerings.
2017rfehf0.name: Guido Leatherface

2017raaanc.author: Justin Lacey
2017raaanc.description:
My Gangrel IC deck has been a staple for a long time. My recent update was
influenced by Martin Weinmayer's NAC deck. Your kill combo is Parity Shift +
Govern the Unaligned + Conditioning. Several fun tricks in the deck. First game
in the tournament, my predator was a power bleed deck. He Pentex Subversioned
my first vampire and then hit me for multiple bleeds for 5. He got me down to 2
pool before I came back to take all the VPs and the Game Win. This deck
survives way better than I expected with considerable pool gain. In the Finals,
I got to choose my predator and prey which gave me an overwhelming advantage.
The deck is a little too dependent on strike: combat ends and I will probably
add a Secure Haven.

Notes:
 Jake Washington	 - The Combo is with Vessel, but generic blood gain is good.
 Metro Underground	 - Fun with Enkil Cog but good after bleeding to setup bleed bounce.
 Pentex Subversion	 - Not great, because you never want to block the (D) action.
 Perfectionist	 - Free Govern the Unaligned.
 Zoo Hunting Ground	 - Two hunting grounds in play is very nice.
 Carlton Van Wyk - One of your best defense cards against Combat rush.
 Form of Mist	 - My ratio of combat cards is something I stole from Martin W.
 Heart of Nizchetus	 - Good, but not necessary.
 Seal of Veddartha	 - Better than the Heart.
 Scourge of the Enochians - played but never mattered.
 Banishment	 - This gets rid of problems and can cause more pool loss than Parity Shift.
 Guard Dogs	 - Fun with Enkil Cog, can get you to long range, and works with bounce.
2017raaanc.name: Big Gangrel

2017stsun0.description:
Bring out Matasuntha asap and play a passive wall early and mid game, keep a low profile.
Block strategically, try to totally destroy at least 1 vampire of your predator as deterrent.
Bleed with Matasuntha when you can, he doesn't need to stay untapped.
When your prey's vampires are all in torpor, bring out a small cap vamp/Imbued to bleed.
Bring out Enkidu for the end game, if you bring him out too early, you lose your low profile and become a serious table threat.
Pool gain is slow, but defense is stable as long as you have Matasuntha ready, helps with keeping a low profile.
Table talk only when needed and don't be too aggressive in table talk, we're keeping a low profile.

2017nqsw.author: Darby Keeney
2017nqsw.description:
Finals seating: Saulot Hide the Heart (Faye, 4th) --> Scobax (Kelly, 1st) --> Khazar (Darby, 2nd) --> Turbo Baron (Fletcher, 5th) --> Daughers Lily Prelude (Raj, 3rd).

An immediate Pentex and bad opening draw shafted the Baron, gaining both Khazar's and Lily Prelude momentum for early VPs - also importantly removing one of the 2 decks that would re-actively screw with minion actions/blood totals.

The game devolved into never-ending Scobax vs lots of actions from 2 players. The Daughters were 1 turn from being ousted pretty much the whole endgame but I had no intention seeing Raj below 6 pool until a few Wraiths reached play or Kelly was ousted. Kelly felt it necessary to Scobax every Wraith attempt, so I was happy to fully occupy his attention and allow Raj's votes to keep Kelly in a defensive bloat/block posture - even when Charming Lobbies hit the table.

The Khazar's deck ended with with no Embraces, no Wraiths, a prey with no library and 5 pool, but holding 1.5vp for the game win from 2nd seed. A postmortem suggested reversing my position with Kelly's might improved his situation, or that opting to bleed (hard) immediately on entering the 3 player game might have yielded a different result. Either way, I felt this was a very well--played final from all involved and enjoyed the game completely.

My copy of Lia Milliner somehow evaporated from the cypt (Graverobbed somewhere?). She's back after seeing omission.

Really needs Master trimming with inclusion of one Direct Intervention - but honestly it was the Liquidations and Embraces that transformed the deck into something worthy of tournament play. With the Liquidations came the need for more MPA, hence Parthenon. Getting to 15 Masters with DI would be optimal.

A mix of rush and defensive minions with a potent anti-equipment twist

Here's the list I played to get 3VP + 2.5vp in the prelims and glorious 0.5VP
in the finals to win the whole deal. The author of the deck is Akseli
Jalava; we switched decks prior to the tournament and I got the better end of
the deal, apparently.

The seating in the finals was:
Matti - weenie Malks with Madness Network and Talbot's Chainsaw (drawing no copies of either in the finals)
Petri - g5-6 Khazar's Diary with lots of Wraith-tech
me - Montano Purge/Mind Rape
Jukka - !Brujah anarch stealth bleed (Undue Influence+Power of One+Spoils of War)
Tommi - Eldest are Kholo breed/boon

2 hours, some passionate discussion and 2 Autarkis Persecutions later, no-one
got ousted, so I won as the highest seed. My game was basically ruined by
Petri's Calrton burning my Montano, but Petri didn't get to do the actions to
put out the wraiths to oust me because of weenie malks with permanent
intercept. Tommi was the closest to be ousted: constant pressure by Jukka's
!Bru bleeders plus 2 Delaying Tactics by Jukka during the same turn got Tommi
to 1 pool before he bounced back to healthy 20-ish pool total in one turn.

I'd suggest dropping Lucita for 3rd Moncada and adding probably at least one
Villein. Camarilla Vitae Slave is cute but not worth the effort. Monastery
should probably be in there, too.

Final table:
Marko (Lasombra Wormwood Baltimorepurge Toolbox) -->
Ilari (Giovanni Powerbleed) -->
Jukka (Dementation Anarch stealth bleed) -->
Jyri (Blackhand Dementation Bleed with Anu Diptinatpa -->
Lauri (me) (Lord Tremere Toolbox)


This was first tournament arrange in one of our new players (Tero Aalto, he
started playing last march, but was already playing at the EC in Genoa) home at
Töölö, Helsinki. Nice residence and works for a small tournaments, with 2-3
tables top. We got 11 players turning up, but one opted to leave before the
start and see the new Star Wars instead, so Thanks to HG for that. We played
two rounds and Final then with 10 players.

Preliminary rounds only had 1GW, in those four games, and that was by Jukka
with 2vp eventhough he was ousted in that game, so all the tables went Time.
Marko won his place in final by coin toss (dice roll) over Henna-Riikka(one of
the two tournament first timers). And Jyri won third seed agianst me in coin
toss (dice Roll). Ilari was second seed (another tournament first timer) and
Jukka with only GW of course was the first seed.

So me and Marko sat at the table, and Jyri opted to bleed me, then Ilari opted
to bleed Jyri and finaly Jukka went between Ilari and Jyri. Marko was diced to
be the starter.

I had personally really bad start and didn't get Malgorzata on starting crypt,
and actually opted to buy new vampire twice before even getting her, and well
so it was turn 5 when I finaly got my first vampire, everyone else had 3-5
minions by that time, and my predator had bled me twice by bleeds of four, so I
really didn't expect to win.

However my predator got enough pressure by his predator that I manage to get
Malgorzata up and Villein, then start using her special ability to bring Lord
Tremere up and Villein him too, even with Wormwood by my prey lowering capacity
down to 7-8.

Even then the Giovanni with four vampires including Le Dinh Tho, manage to oust
his prey and even next one, while my prey with the Lasombra gave a little
pressure to him, finaly allowing me to do timely oust with bleeds and Anarchist
Uprising.

If I had not manage to oust Marko then, I propably would not have survived his
and Ilaris turn, but with that timely oust, I did have the upper hand, and
manage to put all of Ilaris vampires into Torpor and win the came about 10
minutes before time, earning me Tournament win, and my first TWDA entry without
Nana Buruku featured in my decklist.

Winners decklist:

This deck is similar to EC Genoa winners Pau Vilars, so thanks to him and others who had played similar decks before

for a while about losing vote battle to Timo but the arrival of Genevieve (and removal of Noora's Arishat with
her mistress) fixed that. Then it was, luckily, just the matter of bleeding/voting in consistent manner with
enough stealth all the while avoiding the temptation of going to Archonable range. Mainly I have Mikko to
thank for my victory, he built the runway from himself and Lasse and also secured my rear by tripping Noora.

Description: Weenie Animalism wall with a splash of Deflection and Conditioning for the oust.

Final table: Kelly (Baali, Striga, mmpa) > John (weenie Animalism wall) > Kevin (Brandywine Madness Network) > Darby (reply value: large cap vote and bleed) > Brian (large cap Lasombra vote and bleed).

The qualifier went as well as it could have taking into account that most games went to time and only 2 players had a GW going into the final round. We spent some time discussing the cause of this after the tournament and this is what we determined.
-A few players were running lots of votes (Darby and Brian particularly) and butting heads on each referendum. We saw vote cancelling and multiplying tech and several players were using multiple copies of Delaying Tactics.
-Scobax and bleed reduction both had a hand in keeping counters on the table.
-Most players were holding Deflections and the most aggressive decks had huge bleed potential at stealth, so everyone was playing very cautiously while trying to find an opportunity to go forward.

In the end, we had a lot of fun and pick-up games on Friday and Sunday.
Thank you to everyone that came out for this and especially to those that traveled from out of state.

Final table: Henri (Animalism bleed/bock toolbox?) > Lauri (Nergal Powerbleed) > Timo (Arika votes + bleed) > Mikko H. (Arika Mind Rape + bleed + vote) > Niina (New Setite Voter)
Niina 3vp
Lauri 2vp
Nice games overall.. The Finals went so that Timo and Mikko contested Arika, and I managed to oust TImo, after that Mikko's Arika played Mind Rape on my Nergal, but I stil managed to oust him, and after that Henri rushed and torporized my nergal with aggro poke, and then diaplerized, after that we played a long waiting game, where Niina tried to oust Henri and he tried to oust me... finaly about 10 minutes left in game Niina got the upperhand and managed to oust both of us just five mintues to the time. 2016pbdubc.author: Mark Jasper
2016pbdubc.description:
Final table: David Corson-Knowles (Weenie Potence Thrown Gate) > Kate Hanley (Malk 94) > Brett Schofield (Ventrue Anti Obtenebration Vote) > Mark Jasper (Nergal, Saulot and the Great Beast) > Ian Lee (Mid-cap Assamite toolbox?)
Tipping Point: The turn after ousting Ian about 1 hour in I had 3 pool, Unleash Hell's Fury in play,
Saulot with 1 blood and Repulsion, merged Nergal with 3 blood and Call the Great Beast on him already.
Brett (my predator) had 3 ready titled !Ventrue with Obtenebration, vote lock and would surely have ousted me
on his next turn. Dave had 10 pool, 3 tapped weenies (3-5 caps), Carlton untapped and Fame on his prey's vamp
in torpor (Kate had 4-6 pool and Gilbert Duane untapped). After paying 1 pool for Fame and 1 to untap Nergal,
I had 1 pool left. I had Nergal bleed for 3, using his ADV special and the only stealth card in my hand (Mirror Walk)
to get past Carlton. Freak drive. Top decked a Gift of Sleep replacing Freak Drive! Then Saulot Spirit Marionette
bled for 3 with just enough stealth (the Gift of Sleep from hand, repulsion on Saulot) to get past Carlton
and tap him. I had only one Mirror Walk left in my hand, so without the tapping component of Spirit Marionette,
The Great Beast couldn't get past Carlton. Then I popped the Beast on Nergal and bled for 3 to get him to 1.
Dave's own Fame finished him off. With Dave ousted, I had no more fear of getting rushed to death. I had just
enough pool (Brett pressured me hard with KRCs and bounced bleeds from Kate at me the whole game) and the Fury
left to survive another turn of KRCs from Brett and another bounced bleed for 6 from Kate (she stealthed it
by the Fury), to oust Kate and then Brett soon after, completing the table sweep. This was after getting
only 1.5vp in the preliminary rounds and just barely making the final table as the 5th seed. Incredibly
close tournament and my first win!!
2016pbdubc.name: Saulot and Nergal: Beauty and the Beast

2016cdppf0.description:

even less defense considering the intercept problems of the Daughters. Backousting IS an option because there is
very little pool gain (Legal, Wider View and Powerbase if you're lucky to draw it).
The "stealth" module (Daring the Dawn, Missing Voice, Siren's Lure, Paris Opera House and Virtuosa) works extremely well,
even against heavy blocker. Just be sure to use the Daring wisely so you send the blocking minions to torpor.

Description: What if Brum did a Tzimmy Wall?
Typical Tzimisce Wall with my own analysis from the concept, that was created while writing a blog post about errors I see in wall building.

I have no idea why people don't use Vykos ADV as the main vampire in any tzimmy wall. He gives you so many options, like being able to use more Master cards, having one or two silver bullets, etc.

Maybe one less Dreams and one more Guardian Angel. It's fun to have multiple Lodins. And saving blood on Tzimmies is a good thing.
-- Papillon is great here. It clearly was a though on the building of the crypt, since I already would have Vykos Adv.
-- Oddly enough I don't think I need Pentex.

Non arrogant wall.

Ivory Bow is going to leave if I increase Guardian Angels. It is only a win more card.

Odd pick of cards, yes?
-- I don't need Enhanced Senses. Deflecting or canceling referendums is more card effective and beneficial.
-- Everything else is built to protect Smiling Jacks.
-- Wall without ousting power are one of the evils of this World.

Vykos allows for extras in some places.
-- Blood of Acid is good against many things. This pack is perfect for me.

2015dncutn.author: Jonathan van der Smissen
2015dncutn.description:
The deck is just big enough to get you through the table.
1st game: 3vp. My third VP was just when I decked out with 6 minutes left on the clock. Most of my minions were torpored, witouth cards my last one soon joined them and all 4 got eaten.
2nd game: 0vp. Beast rush deck in my back. My deck can't cope with rush Potence Torn Grapple Blur.
3rd game: 3vp. A crucial seduction on anneke allowed my first oust. My prey and predator were contesting a Pentex for the whole game. Martin's Presence bleeder got through the wakes of anneke anson after which I took the table.

Final: Setite corrupt vote -> Nosferatu vote -> Gangrel royalty -> me Kiasyd sb -> Presence bleed.
My opening crypt at this table was perfect. I had Pherydima (8 bishop) and Omme (7 priscus) 4 transfers to start with and a Govern.
Me and the Nosferatu had votelock over my predator which allowed me to keep the Gangrel alive but severely damaged and a little threat. I got through the Presence deck, at which point the table started to collapse. The Nosferatu died soon after. Giving me, the stealth bleed deck votelock over the table. I went from 14 to 4 pool in a single turn, allowing myself to get Parity Shifted for my predators benefit, pentexing xaviar(who downgraded to prince) influencing a new minion and paying Pherydima to get an untapped minion.

I delayed the Reckless Agitation from the setites who were about to backoust me.
Then my predator did a bleed of 1 with form of mist (3 pool left) he tried to cycle hard to find his kine resources contested , luckily he failed to find it.
My prey had 3 pool left, my predator 7.
My prey bounces the first Govern, bounces the second Govern. I go for a third and luckily that's all he had. Bleed for 1 with a seduction to win the game.

2015lcqwp0.description:
I believe this is the list I won Last Chance with. Maybe someone from the EC organizers can check that the
tournament details and the decklist are correct (as I already disassembled the deck back in the EC and
there's no list other than the one I gave to judges)?

The deck itself has the usual suspects with AUS PRE. It is inspired by a similiar deck popularized by
Martin Weinmeyer's EC win back in 2009 - although with higher caps, more Auspex and lacking Fortitude and
Daring the Dawns. This version has problems with dedicated blockers and stealth vote, but otherwise has
proven to be quite resilient with lots of reactions and combat ends, which gives the flexibility to alter
your tempo and possibly wait for an opportunity to present itself.

In the preliminary rounds I really would have needed Darings against my ani pro prey. In the second round
I got lucky as Kim was one card short of running away with the game, which would have costed me the spot
in the finals. And I got lucky again in the finals drawing half of my combat ends in the first quarter of
the library against Pascal's Enkidu - but some luck is obviously needed in this game. In the heads-up
against Noora's Unnamed the deck transformed into a half-decent block deck.

2015nrqwri.author: Matthew Morgan
2015nrqwri.description:
Description: This deck originally had one Monastery of Shadows, but I must have moved it to another deck or something. Basically what you have here is an Edward Vignes deck where everybody costs 4 extra pool. The nice thing about all those titles is you can try to shut down bloat vote. Adding pool to the table is bad. I made this deck because I hadn't won a tournament with Ventrue yet (never had an Arika phase) and because I've lost my fear of being ousted and now just play a lot of offense. Haven't had a game go to time in quite a while.

Anyway, the deck took 15 of 19 potential VPs all day, which might be a personal best. I let two get away in the first round because Peteo used some kind of mind control on me and convinced me he had wakes when he didn't. I then took 4vp on a pair of 5 player tables and swept the final, mostly by letting bad things happen to people who weren't me. All three of my preliminary rounds finished first and the final took around an hour.

13 cards makes me feel better about not being crypt screwed and empirical evidence has supported that, but there's no real math behind it.

Daring the Dawn was key in the final. Seduction is also very important. I got Enkil Cog out every time I drew it.

Haven't gotten this card to do anything useful for me.

Ephor is really just there for flavor, but has helped a little from time to time.

I kept outsmarting myself and not being able to Parity Shift but having the most pool is a pretty good problem to have. I could see swapping a Parity Shift for Banishment. Great for dealing with the untapped bouncer.
2015nrqwri.name: Payload

2015tfnwri.author: Jennifer Hirsch
2015tfnwri.description: The deck worked well when it got going, but getting going from the #2 position at a table was tough. After playing it more, I'd put in a second Secure Haven, remove Honor the Elders for another damaging vote (not enough big vamps out to make it worth while) and change out at least one True Love's Face for Voter Captivation - the deck needs bloat and that (and Villein) are all it has. Mundane was really helpful when I drew it, and I'd probably swap one of the Telepathic Misdirection or Counters for another Majesty. Finally, Drozodny is amazing, if I didn't need votes, he beat Stavros every time.

2014nacday2co.author: Matthew Hirsch
2014nacday2co.description:
Description: It's a vote deck with a lot of toolbox, defense, and agg strikes.
Notes:
I originally had built a tournament-level Terrifisto deck, and I also had a
Lambach deck in my casual deck supply (which used goofy stuff like Deploy the Hand).
I played the Terrifisto deck at the LCQ #1, and I found it to be quite
underwhelming. So I started a deck retrofit the morning of the tournament,
using the Lambach crypt, and the Terrifisto library. Removing ~8 Fortitude cards from
the Terrifisto deck gave me some creative space to work with.

Even for a crypt that has great access to untap and intercept
effects, putting an Under Siege on the table is really powerful. I simply get
the freedom to tap out and my predator knows I have untap/intercept sitting on
the table. Add Lambach's agg threat on top of that.

If he gets stolen, he can trash the Black Forest Base. I know
it's a bit corner case, but you do have to watch out for it. Otherwise you're
going to endure some serious gloating when someone actually pulls it off.

It's been said before, but it's worth repeating:
This card is amazingly good and other players don't even see how you're building
the perfect hand at the start of your turn. This card directly got me the winning
VP, as I drew into two Changelings at just the right time.

I like this card, but it's very hard to remember to use it
in every untap phase (including your own) For some reason I had particular trouble
remembering to use it in my prey's untap phase.

This is a great card, but I'm always hesitant to add it
to decks because it adds table chatter. If you use it, be prepared for the
cross-table begging and have a ready yes/no answer prepared so it doesn't
stall the game.
2014nacday2co.name: Unknown

2014rmbmg0.author: Johannes Walch
2014rmbmg0.description:
This deck is sort of an evolution of my !Nos Deck centered around Cailean
where I have big vampires that fight really well and have a good defense
but had problems with consistently getting gamewins due to the slow build up
(few crypt acceleration) and lack of multi-act. I cut back on the fight
consistency and fixed those two problems.
The master section is completely focused on crypt acceleration and pool gain.
There are lots of obvious and helpful additions like Fame, but really there
is no way to fit them without sacrificing something.
The Biothauma Experiments are really strong and the mini equipment module
works well. I thought about going for more fancy silver bullets, but in the
end the basic stuff is far more useful. Never used the Dog Pack, good in
theory against Majesty heavy preys.
Enkil Cog is a no brainer and I usually use at least two or none, the six
Freak Drives are just right, more will easily be too much. Don't need to
constantly multi-act, rather in a few strategic places (like putting on an
experiment and then Deep Song).
The combat is diverse on purpose to keep people guessing, especially since
the discipline spread of the vamps is scary. It is also focused around not
spending blood, none of the cards cost, and there is multiple synergies in
there. I can't consistenly win against combat heavy decks but I can survive
the one or two critical combats and have some hitback and I can usually
obliterate anything that doesn't fight at all.

Anarch Converts saved me in both preliminary games - one of the walls was using
Anarch Revolt to do pool damage...

Finals - I used my predator's lunge to deflect to my prey and wear his defenses down.
A Pentex on his remaining vampire allowed me to oust. We timed out 2 minutes 15 seconds
later. That gave me the only VP at the table...
2013sofsvqsjc.event: Show of Force Silicon Valley Qualifier
2013sofsvqsjc.name: Khazar's Diary deck ripped from TWDA

2013vampspb.author: Roberto Mautone Junior
2013vampspb.description:
Deck Description: Vote / Rush Deck that uses the pool of other players to buy weapons,
and rush all vampires. After that, bleed with New Carthage. Persistent block always
get unaware predators with no combat ends, giving chance to table dominance.
Long Live to the Brujah!
2013vampspb.name: Carthage is the New Rome!

Otso Saariluoma's deck with minor modifications.

2013jrxxmjhf.description:

Put the Perfectionist on Anu and then just hunt or bounce with her. Remember that you can
use Thuggees to Veil your other minions. Do the dirty work with !Malks.
2013jrxxmjhf.name: Black Hand + Thuggees & Anu

2013nmftwpf.description:
Description: Accordingly to its creator, the deck was focused on tapping vampires
with Deep Song, then untapping with Earth Meld...
2013nmftwpf.name: The tap and bleed strategy

2013eotd5lbhf.author: Tuuli Myllynen
2013eotd5lbhf.description:
Francois recruits Ossian the Yoda style, and takes an oust
when the rest of the table take their time bickering and
arguing amongst themselves. When you're on a [love] boat,
the tournaments are won with love, not war!
2013eotd5lbhf.event: Eyes of the Dead 5: Love Boat
2013eotd5lbhf.location: M/S Silja Serenade ferry between Stockholm and Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland
2013eotd5lbhf.name: Hmm, a werewolf I can has!

2013anzccsa.author: Peter Rophail
2013anzccsa.description:
Description: A 2013 incarnation of the deck I used to
win the 2005 Australian Championships. This deck never
seems to do much, but is very effective. Table play is
critical, especially early on. Most VP's scored by "lunging"
(with Pentex Subversion) or by combat late in the game. Very
difficult to oust, especially if allowed to set up. The absolute
key is to use Magic of the Smith to bring out the Heart as
early in the game as possible. From there you have most tables
covered.
2013anzccsa.name: The Quiet Achiever 2013

2013anzlcqpa.author: Nick Miller
2013anzlcqpa.event: AUSNZ Continental Championship 2013 - Last Chance Qualifier
2013anzlcqpa.name: Sha-Ennu bleed

2013ecd1ss.author: Martin Weinmayer
2013ecd1ss.name: EC 2013 Day 1: Stanislava & Friends Dom/For Bleed/Vote

2013ecsodss.author: Patrick Benoit
2013ecsodss.description:
I'm not sure that's the shilmulo tarot is usefull. It could be
replaced by a last stand, but I'm not sure it won't create flow
problems. The rumors is here to get a better flow and also to
play something like a Pentex Subversion before playing Week of
Nigthmares. Consanguinous condemnation is here to tap some minions
your prey keeps untapped to block but also and firstly to deflect.
It could also be defensive by calling it just before a consanguinous
boon if you know that's someone is keeping an untapped vampire to
play delaying tactics. And it's also good to call a domain challenge
just after. If everything is ok, you should be able to put week of
nightmares in turn 6-7 with nearly 12-16 minions.
2013ecsodss.name: Mozambiqué

2013woabss.author: Petteri Teerikangas
2013woabss.description:
Description: Unnamed deck using Maleficia; Greater Curses for
gaining more pool and slowing down combat decks, evil eyes
canceling and psalms to get bleeds in right address. Deck needs
some slimming down and maybe some Villeins as vampires where in
near full capacity in many games I played in boat and EC. Thanks
for building tips (and few borrowed cards) for Toni Karjalainen.
2013woabss.location: M/S Silja Symphony (ferry between Helsinki and Stockholm), Stockholm, Sweden
2013woabss.name: Unnamed cruising at Baltic Sea

2013dncun0.author: Bram Van Stappen
2013dncun0.description:
Since most of the times your prey and grandprey make deals for bleeds of one
and it's impossible to eagle's sight everything, I thought it might be worthwhile
to try and prevent your prey from playing at all... so Brainwash, Pentex for something
that comes out, a bit of defense and an occasional eagle's sight. Ashur to recover
removed 419, intercept and the small amount of combat. And a last stand that I pulled
off to play in the second game, so your grandprey doesn't get the pool you have on the 419s.

2013fcqf14pf.author: Rudolf Scholz
2013fcqf14pf.description: Description: Avec en merci beaucoup à Kamel Senni
2013fcqf14pf.name: Maris et Lutz à Paris

2013jr19siphf.event: Justicar Retribution XIX - Swinging in Pain
2013jr19siphf.name: Lasombra S&B

2013flcqpf.description: You're a girl and you don't have any shampoo
2013flcqpf.name: T'es une fille et tu n'as pas de shampoing

2013mmbh.author: Csaba Greguss
2013mmbh.description:
Description: "A liitle bit of this, a little bit of that... I missed
one or two Conductors for the deck, never used the Reinforcements,
having all the vampires out all rounds, Bane+ Phantom + stealth are
sweet against blockers, definitely there is space for 1-2 additional
Siren's Lure."
2013mmbh.name: Modern Daughters

2013taolmi.author: Simone Zanni
2013taolmi.description:
Description: It's a toolbox recursive deck, with some situational strong
defense and a light necrobleed module to oust. Extremely valuable had been
the 2 Trochomancy to take care of other recursive decks, and the combo
Revelations/Precision to get rid of a double Deflection in my prey's hand.
Sacre Coeur never been much useful due to the lack of ally deck, but I will
keep it. Nicomedes is AMAZING when you have 11/12 cards in hand, and
Sennadurek skill has often been underestimated, giving me full acces to
almost all table's hand.
2013taolmi.name: Guillaume for rent

2013lichs0.author: Tomas Wallmur
2013lichs0.description:
SB with Hotel. Govern down until you have enough minions then bleed.
Yes I know its kinda revoloutionary, but give it a try.
2013lichs0.name: The Hotelkedja

2013tsclp0.author: Marcin Szybkowski
2013tsclp0.description:
Description: This deck is designed to bring out War Ghouls at extra
speed - cutting the deck size to 50 and using D'habi Revenants does
the trick nicely, plus the revenants make perfect "meat" for corrupt
constructs later on. Ideally you should have 3-4 minions on turn 3,
which is not uncommon. Guedado is a true star here, giving you access
to the Powerbase, Forgotten Labyrinths and of course the Strange day,
which literally saved the day many times. Some credit goes to Szewski
for his advices before playing my 1st tournament with this deck. Thanks mate.
2013tsclp0.event: Lodz by Night - The Second Coming
2013tsclp0.name: Guedado Ghouls

2013ccpdms.author: Alejandro Pérez Rosselló
2013ccpdms.description: Played and modified by: Alejandro Pérez Rosselló
2013ccpdms.name: Nephandus Swarm

2013jbllac.event: Jann Berger's "L" is for Lunatic Eruption

refill 'em a bit. Do stuff, block stuff, fight stuff. Watch out
for Basilia - she's got agg hands!
2013jbilac.name: Basilia Gives Aids

2013acc.author: Bann Lum
2013acc.description:
Should have replaced all of my crypt to 11-Cap Vampires
(except 3x Halim Bey and Ahmose Chambers)
Need to test using Dreams of the Sphinx instead of
Fragment of the Book of Nod.

GW3 + GW5 + 3vp in final

2013tsiems.name: Trolls Converters

2013jr18hwthf.author: Janne Hägglund
2013jr18hwthf.description:
Description: I've been playing variations of this same deck
since my 2007 "Twist with Conviction".

Tournaments are Serious Business, so my Imbued have ditched
their wacky infernal friends (with their Maleficia/Evil Eye
or Striga/Scobax module). They still love to hack computers
though, since that seriously speeds up their stealth bleeding.

Things I would change:
- Remove all but one On the Qui Vive.
- Wendell Delburton was useless. I forgot to take him out
after reducing the number of Weighted Walking Sticks by a lot.
- Suddens or Washes would be nice.
2013jr18hwthf.event: Justicar Retribution XVIII - Hard Without Tenderness
2013jr18hwthf.name: Imbued nerds no longer worship Satan

2013bissp0.author: Adam Hulse
2013bissp0.description:
Description: A Mata Hari + kholo deck (created by Adam Hulse and
Sonam Adinolf). Sonam tried a version of this deck in 2012 Origins
and it was determined that there was not enough payload. So I made
the deck 90 cards and upped the KRC by a lot. The Mask of 1000 Faces
are in there to get around no stealth for the weenie Laibon. Mata masks
and then plays faceless. I didn't make it work so well so that combo
needs some more play to see if worth it.
2013bissp0.name: Mata Hari Is the Founder

2013bssbotuk.author: Hugh Angseesing
2013bssbotuk.name: Gents on the town, twirling their canes v7 2013

2013ukdcp0.author: Maciej Kozlowski
2013ukdcp0.description:
This deck was based on Mathieu Rivero's TWD, limited by my access to cards
(one more copy of the HoN should really be here) and slightly optimised
with other cards I thought would play nicely. Performance inspired by the
tips on the grinder decks from the Cause and Effect show on YT. Many thanks
to all of you guys!
2013ukdcp0.name: Owain's Grindhouse

2013nbobluk.author: Boris Mailhé
2013nbobluk.description:
An old deck slightly tweaked after looking at Kakarot and Lönkka's TWDs.
DOM and permanent +1 Stealth is amazing, and an early Heart of Nizchetus
allows to run a huge Wash + reactions package without sacrificing the
offensive cardflow. So you can afford to take it slowly, Govern your
whole uncontrolled region out, tool up and wait for the opening.
2013nbobluk.name: DOM, +1 stealth, what else?

2013hnqgh0.author: Péter Botos
2013hnqgh0.description:
Inspired by "Snakes on the Plane" by Ivan Marin-Rivas.
This deck, however, relies more on Maleficia for defensive
purpuses as well. Rather slow to build up but can be very
effective with time. What I discovered during the games that
putting one Barrenness on one or two key vampires can very
much slow down other decks by limiting their capability to
Govern out company, play Enkil Cog, etc.
Went up to 90 library cards to include two copies of sense the
sin for solid ousting power and three Dreams for better cards
flow. Both turned out to be a good idea - thanx to Martin Major.
2013hnqgh0.name: Cybele's Curse v2

2013jr17hf.author: Matias Frosterus
2013jr17hf.description:
Group 4 Ahrimanes make for an excellent Animalism focused,
mid-cap crypt with good Spiritus defense and some Presence
boosted bleed ability.
2013jr17hf.event: Justicar Retribution XVII - Leave the Best Behind
2013jr17hf.name: Ahrimane Animalism Balanced Approach

2013hnqbhj.author: Péter Botos
2013hnqbhj.description:
Inspired by "Snakes on the Plane" by Ivan Marin-Rivas. This deck, however,
relies more on Maleficia for defensive purposes as well. Rather slow to
build up but can be very effective with time. What I discovered during the
games that putting one Barrenness on one or two key vampires can very much
slow down other decks by limiting their capability to Govern out company,
play Enkil Cog, etc.
2013hnqbhj.name: Cybele's Curse

2013vcqma0.author: Steve Van Nus
2013vcqma0.description:
Description: Deck designed to get weenies princes out quick, parity's for
pool damage/gain which also gives strong deal making power. Brujah Debates
for defence/offence, hopefully making prey/predator thinking twice before
blocking. Has a some combat so you hopefully don't get totally pole-axed
when table starts working together to remove Debates (which happens).
Immortal Grapples are there to keep other decks that pack strike combat/dodge
decks (and no prevention) nervous about blocking, & Blood Dolls in there to
reduce your pool if prey is staying under Parity Shift range, and for
blood/pool management. Carthage Remembered + computer hacking worked well
in one game. Second Tradition for block defence worked well.

Card's I'd take out: Well-Aimed Car (placed in there for shits & giggles,
never got to use), would replace for Stunt Cycle or Sew Lid. Would take out
1 Pulled Fang and replace with 1 Disarm (grappled and disarmed Anneke after
she blocked cross table as she kept voted down most of what I did-which
is understandable).

Possible additions: Another Dreams of the Sphinx, Smiling Jack,
Specialization, Parthenon (I could not find any I owned otherwise
on the day I would have had 3-4 in deck).
2013vcqma0.event: Victorian Qualifier for the AUSNZ Continental Championship
2013vcqma0.name: Brujah Mass Debate

2013gecqlg.author: Andreas Nusser
2013gecqlg.description:
Winner of the German ECQ 2013. So far I have played this deck for 6 games.
3 Game Wins and some VPs in the other games. Seems pretty solid deck
construction to me and the cards are very balanced. Miller is important
but not a key vampire that you have to rely uopn.

Fleetness are great in combination with Palla Grande. Always had enough
forward pressure. Art Scams were extremelly important for blood gain and
saved me a lot of times.
2013gecqlg.name: "Tai Chi Walking Stick Form" by Miller & his students

2013fcqco0.author: Kym Alishahi
2013fcqco0.description: Description: "The deck that made Drace quit VTES"
2013fcqco0.name: Kym Alishahi's Drace IS The unnamed

2013d2stco.description: Description: Same as my E2012 Day2 deck, with two more cards
2013d2stco.name: Better Gents, Same Sticks, In America

2013nacd2co.description: Description: Get out Jacob and an Akunanse. Stay sober. Win.
2013nacd2co.name: Team Jacob

2013nacd1co.author: Bill Troxel
2013nacd1co.description:
3GW (in 3R+F)
Description: This is a "training" deck that I made for a new player
that sometimes played with my group.
2013nacd1co.name: Meshenka 101

2013lnlcqco.author: Tiago Brum
2013lnlcqco.description:
Description: Been using the version that the European Champion used,
with some changes acording to my playstyle and the Portuguese environment.
Still think the deck needs a couple of Delaying Tactics, but what to take out?
2013lnlcqco.name: Girls Will Find Revelations in America

2013lcqco0.author: Randal Rudstam
2013lcqco0.description:
3GW


Description: I got the original idea from Anders Löf. He was running it
with Nana and Ashur rush combat without reaction cards. I decided that I
wanted to run it with Aksinya with reactions instead. The decks are quite
different but the idea with high amount of Pentex(TM) works kinda the same.
2013lcqco0.name: Girls in the Pentex(TM) boardroom

2013wone20.author: Randal Rudstam
2013wone20.description:
This deck is a a remake of a deck that Ivan Marin-Rivas runs in Stockholm.
I was a few cards short so I decided to add the Ashurs angle to it.
2013wone20.name: The hot pot

2013wone10.author: Mikkel Petersen
2013wone10.description: Description: Get out Jacob and an Akunanse. Stay sober. Win.
2013wone10.name: Team Jacob

2013bldhf0.author: Matias Frosterus
2013bldhf0.description:
Description: Matthew makes the Master selection a lot cheaper
making it easy to live with the Scarce penalty. Having your prey
tap out every turn is nice at which point you can just bleed while
juggling your permanents with the Heidelberg. The Dreams and the
Aura Readings prevent hand jams.
2013bldhf0.event: Justicar Retribution XVI - Bela Lugosi's Dead
2013bldhf0.name: Matthew and Serenna Play with Marionettes

2013clacrm.author: Matthew Morgan
2013clacrm.description:
Description: It's bad medicine because leeches and Molotov cocktails
are bad for you and will not make you well.

Goal: Antonio and one other guy. There's no reason to get more than two
vampires. Extra pool is for Nephandi.

Two Havens are not enough. Needs at least four. The Rack was probably
stolen from some other deck at some point.

I really like Leech. Only blocked once all day and it was by Jake.

One Conditioning?!? Uh, yeah missing cards. Should be around four.

A few times before when I played this deck I found myself in the
odd position of having enough pool but being out of Nephandi.
Didn't happen this time though.

Delaying Tactics needed!
2013clacrm.event: Crusade: London and Copenhagen - Maryland NAC Qualifier
2013clacrm.name: Bad Medicine

2013sosp.author: Dawid Cyran
2013sosp.description:
It's a deck I've been playing with for some time now. The third version of it,
or even the fourth one. I enhance it every now and then.
2013sosp.name: Nakhthorheb and Mummies

2013pbspb0.author: Felipe Fiuza
2013pbspb0.description: Description: Just Be cool, Block, and Wait.
2013pbspb0.name: La ostia

2013jbhlac.author: Robert Goudie
2013jbhlac.description:
The cool trick of the deck is to use the play of a Heaven's Gate
to reset the Trap counters and continue the combat (the minions
in combat do not need to be the ones playing cards to reset a trap).
2013jbhlac.name: Nike Cult

2013jbglac.author: Julien Guérand
2013jbglac.name: Even the War Ghouls Look Nervous

2013lwtuahf.author: Marko Lindroos
2013lwtuahf.event: Justicar Retribution XV - Love Will Tear Us Apart
2013lwtuahf.name: Lilith ain't blessing anymore, but Dmitra can give you a kiss

2013c2cp.author: Piotr Jaworski
2013c2cp.description: To rape, or not to rape...
2013c2cp.name: Unknown

2013jbflac.author: Robert Goudie
2013jbflac.description:
Based on Ference Vasadi's Ravnos Deck
Resilient Deck that just refused to die. In the finals I
had to play the Week of Nightmares much earlier than I would
have liked. Ousted my prey but within a few turns the Week
of Nightmares counters would all expire and slam my vamps.
Took the opportunity to rearrange my blood a bit via Vessel
and then blew up the Week on my own turn so that I could
control things a bit. By ordering those effects I saved one
vamp and was able to hold on for the victory.
2013jbflac.name: Draba Jack

2013jbelac.author: Brandon Haas
2013jbelac.description:
Inspired by old school Gangrel bleed decks, tailored for the
LA environment. Great way to bleed for 8 on a budget. 5vp in
the final, including two I got in one turn.
2013jbelac.name: Budget Stanislava

2013rr5pf0.author: Vincent Ripoll
2013rr5pf0.description:
Description: Locked within the walls of the Abbey of Mount
Zion (Monastery of Shadows), Giotto Verducci uses the Fragments
brought back from Kaymakli to attract and organize a secret
meeting between the leaders of the Ventrue Clan.
2013rr5pf0.name: With a little help from Giotto

2013nycqnyc.author: Adam Hulse
2013nycqnyc.description:
Description: New York City Qualifier Tournament Deck Winner 2013
A Tzimisce Vote deck. A nice thing is that when going against them,
you never know what you are facing. Bounce? Combat? Bleed? I knew
that i would be seeing some Cam vote decks in there so Private
Audience and Fear of Mekhet were a must. Purchase Pact barely
made the cut but I figured with Radu I should try it. It even
works in torpor! And instead of a variety of combat, I went back
to good ole' agg + Rötschreck.
2013nycqnyc.name: Terrifying Politics

2013h2hh.author: David Litwin
2013h2hh.description:
Description: After getting obliterated in the first tournament by
voting decks I broke out one of mine I had been trying on JOL with
on and off success. After a fair showing in R1&2 the deck took
advantage of a great series of turns late in the final. Early on
it got rushed into the ground by Deep Song and spent midgame rescuing
and hunting, while taking a shot at its prey when able. After the ANI
rush had to go upstream the deck got a turn and ousted the next 3 preys
with 3 consecutive KRCs, with the ANI not able to dunk enough vampires
in the all but meaningless last few turns. The deck has trouble with
any real intercept and the Sacrifice was used twice by Kyle Strathcona
to kill a Neighbor John.
2013h2hh.name: All of a Sudden

2013h1hh.author: Dan Apholz
2013h1hh.description:
Modified from an early deck borrowed from David it provides
enough stealth to beat light intercept and voting power to
get votes though. During each round the deck ran into little
in the way of strong intercept or opposing voters. Each game
the initial prey and predator were unable to produce enough
intercept and opposing voters too few to overcome votes or
handle Scalpel Tongues or vote push. Would reconsider adding
Klaus back in as a 4th minion as the deck can easily get a
4th minion into play if given the time.
2013h1hh.name: Mr Clean

2013ecqbotuk.author: Ke Carlton
2013ecqbotuk.description:
Description: Switched Legal's to Intimidation for blood management,
also added 1x Coven and Jake - reduced Lilith's to 1x copy as not
really needed now. Deck is quite low on stealth, but permastealth
and corruption counters offset that. Cagliostro is awesome when paired
with Nakhhorheb and the extra discard phase is great to avoid hand jams.
Minimal bounce, but having Keith untapped generally discourages big bleeds.
Added extra Majesties and Mental Mazes for UK meta. Could do with 1x Golconda.
2013ecqbotuk.name: Eternal Abuse

2013grm3tbjf.author: Petrus Makkonen
2013grm3tbjf.description:
Basically, I just wanted to abuse Lilith's Blessing before it
got banned in VEKN sanctioned tournaments. Also, G2-3 Ventrue
are really really cool and I had never played them before.
I'd rather have a second Arika instead of a third Marcus Vitel,
but I didn't own any.
2013grm3tbjf.event: The Garou Rim Monthly III: The Blowtorcher
2013grm3tbjf.name: Goodbye Lilith's Blessings

2013nunui0.author: Giulio Grimaldi
2013nunui0.event: Italian Qualifier Tour - Nightmares Upon Nightmares
2013nunui0.name: Unknown

2013ecqoc0.author: Goran Damjanic
2013ecqoc0.description: Description: Recycled Deck from 2012 - 3GWs in 3 Rounds. Giovanni Powerbleed
2013ecqoc0.name: Le Giovanni

2013etaomss.author: Erik Mossberg
2013etaomss.description:
Bakr is more important than I thought, I got him in the final
luckily and he played a big part, so I should add 2 copies.
I should also remove minimum two master cards (Path of Blood
and Hunting Ground).

2013jbdifd.author: Aaron Clark
2013jbdifd.description:
Description: It won a tournament, but can it win a game?
Angelica's special means that Ascendances can be used for
intercept as well as pool gain. She gets Eternal Vigilance
and a .44 Magnum and blocks. Anson provides support, cycling
masters faster and providing Angelica with blood from the
Fifth Tradition. Fish for weenies, stealth bleed or bruise
bleed for the VP.

I felt perpetually short on bleed during the tournament,
and after having written out the decklist, I see that I
had fewer bleed cards than I thought. At minimum, one
Shroud of Night should be switched for a Threats. One of
the Ascendances probably should be changed to a Pentex
Subversion for contesting or lunging, but Pentex is less
prevalent in L.A. than in other places.
2013jbdifd.name: Angelica Ascendant

2013jbcifc.author: Dennis Lien
2013jbcifc.description:
This was one hairy final. I was down to 1 pool like 3 times.
I ended up killing my prey with a shift and finished off my grand
prey by Justicar Retributioning his main vamp. If I ran this
again, I'd definitely run 4 shifts and 4 boons instead.
Keep on bleedin.
Peace
Dennis E. Lien
2013jbcifc.name: The 7th Tradition: Parity Shift

2013pst610.author: Matti Palomäki
2013pst610.description:
Tap-and-bleed deck that uses CrimethInc. at tha to take actions before bleeding.
The key to the final was to sit away from the aus-weenies and to start moving forwards at
the right moment, ie. when I could oust my prey and the aus-weenies in one turn. I've had
this deck assembled since Twilight Rebellion came out. It's been tweaked and played every
once in a while, and at the moment I'm pretty happy with it.
2013pst610.name: the unaligned revolutionaries

2013tswri0.author: Kym Alishahi
2013tswri0.description:
(Special thanks to Drace Zhan for introducing me to Alonzo
Guillen as an addition to the crypt)
The purpose of this Cock Robin/Deep Song/Enkil Cog iteration is
to greatly boost that deck archetype's versatility by taking
advantage of the powerful support abilities of Shahid and Alonzo
Guillen. Extra hand size/hand building combined with being able
to see predator/prey hands is the reason I call it the espionage
network because like good secret service networks in the world the
deck can see exactly what its target is doing and act accordingly.
It can be played in a variety of ways depending on the table.
2013tswri0.name: Cock Robin Espionage Network

2013tfwri0.author: Kevin Mullen
2013tfwri0.description:
This is one of the first decks I made. It was very rewarding to finally
win a tournament with it. As the Boston VTES group will tell you, I'm
the Miller guy. This deck has undergone an evolution from a committed
intercept combat deck, to a bleed deck emphasizing Palla Grande and a
combat package to discourage blocking. Focus on high efficiency permanents
allows the deck to mostly focus on reactions and combat. If you replicate
this deck make sure to spread the damage masters and bow amongst your
minions so other players don't want to block them. Punching with Miller
for 4 is fun, but doesn't get you GWs.
2013tfwri0.name: Miller Time

2013vinnss.description:

Obtenebration and Dominate. No way of taking blood off of Vampires
since they tend to use it for playing the cards. Nocturns help against
rush and allowed for a high amount of On the Qui Vive and therefore
Redirections compared to Deflections. The name comes from me when
people expected the deck to be full of mytherceria cards.
2012yofhf0.name: This Isn't That Kind of a Deck, Honest!

2012gtusjc.author: Dennis Lien
2012gtusjc.description:
This is a modification of an old deck idea where I tried to have
Tariq "atone" and block everything. This version is much more
balanced and simply tries to use Tariq's abilities with the possiblity
of an Atonement. I can already see a few flaws in the design.
I think I'll dump the Necromancy and Anima Gathering angles and
just put in more reactions and action mods.

I was very fortunate to win the tourney. It was a really fun final
and very competitive. David Anderson as my prey looked like he had
it until Brett "archoned" his Mu-aziz. I lost Tariq to Brett's Carlton
but was able to bleed out David with what I had left and hold on until
the game timed out.
2012gtusjc.name: Extremely Silent and Incredibly Far Away

2012pnclp0.author: Tiago Brum
2012pnclp0.description:
Description: Govern Superior as much as possible.
Most times, people don't see this deck as the table threat, even after 4 minions.
I think it's because players have irrational fears of stealth, big cap vampires,
players with vote lock, pure rush, walls...
I'm happy with list. Almost the same list that I took to the Final of EC 2012.

Crypt is fine.
Mary Anne Blaire is bad in this deck. Takes a long time to influence and would
require Freak Drives to use properly. Rather have 2 vampires by the same time
I would have Mary.

Consciously not using Scourge of the Enochians in the EC was probably
one of my worse mistakes in VtES ever.

14 is the new 10

Great card here. 90% of the time, used for bleed, but even more useful
those 10% of times you need to bounce a Giovanni or Kiasyd mega bleeder.

The quantity of bounce allows for the combat to be more offensive.
Second Tradition and Lodin are even more awesome together.
Might add an 8th Second Tradition.
2012pnclp0.name: Better Gents, Same Sticks, No Parity Shifts. Ever.

2012jr11hf.author: Heikki Palomäki
2012jr11hf.description:
Description: Shameless obf dom S&B. A lot of titles for table control
and vote protection. There is also a sizable reaction package for bleed
defence. Using Murmur of the False Will as main defence gives this deck
a great advantage, not only because it can be used for bleeding and
bouncing, but because it is free. Vampires can be Villeined to very
little blood as Governs are almost only ways of losing blood.
This deck is obviously very vulnerable to rushes but votes work pretty
well as protection against diableries as well. Secure Haven, Golconda,
Reins of Power and Obediences would be great additions to this deck but
it would require taking something else out.
2012jr11hf.name: Heavy duty

2012fncrf0.author: Vincent Ripoll
2012fncrf0.description:
I got some inspiration from Aleksi Nuora's TWD to build this one.
Protean and Celerity are great costless polyvalent combat disciplines
(there are only 3 Claws that cost blood amongst the 60 combat cards).
I playtested and tweaked it lots of time during our weekly session
(thanks to my patient victims) and I'm quite happy about it.

Enkidu in 5 copies sometimes didn't show up. I added one copy (with a 13-crypt card to draw more side-kicks)

Master come quite quickly because you cycle lots of cards. You can even
-- jam with master even there are only 12 of them, but it's quite rare.
2012fncrf0.name: Enkidu PRO CEL

2012twtiahf.author: Aleksi Nuora
2012twtiahf.description:
Description: Bring out big guys with Zillah's to secure a fast vote lock,
proceed to win with Undele. For defending and breaking stalemates, pull dick
moves like recycling Banishment, DI, Entrancement or Pentex. Very difficult
to stop by the time it gets a third minion out.
The burn option cards are a mix of whatever I had within arm's reach at the
time I built the deck. Ideally, they would all be masters to feed Anthelios.
The deck needs a sixth Villein in order to draw one reliably and early,
probably in place of Golconda or Giant's Blood. If I was expecting heavy
bleeding I would also add a second Protected Resources.
2012twtiahf.event: Justicar Retribution IX - The Winner Takes it All
2012twtiahf.name: Undele's Bag of Dicks

2012lcqdcdf.author: Thomas Gibson
2012lcqdcdf.description:

enkil, then bleed for 8. Slow bleed stealth deck with good bloat and
very resilient to rush - especially strong in an Animalism/Celerity-gun
environment.
2012lcqdcdf.name: Wicked Bleed
