2012rrm.author: Matthew Morgan
2012rrm.description:
Description: Won DC qualifier September 22, 2012.

Never saw the Ventrue at all in four rounds but otherwise
had good crypt draws.

Villein always clumped but otherwise enabled the deck.
I Pacted Orlando for Presence a couple of times and
voter capped with him for about 15 once. I wouldn't
consider it an integral component though.

Could have played a couple Entrancements,
but they wouldn't have helped.

Anything missing? I don't think so.
This all worked really well.

Could have had more stealth but I didn't ever face
heavy intercept as my prey. I had a wall in the
predator position round 2 and got blocked a bit,
but I basically just took the table by bleeding
forward.

Maybe too much. Bloat and payload is what this deck is about.

Torrent was never played. Probably not a good choice
for this deck as there isn't enough CEL.

Didn't have a lot of use for these. I love Scalpel Tongue
but didn't need it often. REG is a great card for Toreador,
but unplayable by Orlando.
2012rrm.name: Torelando

2012cecq.author: David Sniegon
2012cecq.description:
About deck- block, block, block... work on poolgain, try to get
Magnum on Ira as fast as you can and keep Rack/Vessel/Montreal
for pools... its good idea to put Rack+2 Vessel on Yvette/Sabrina
and just stand and block and gain pools... well worked for me perfectly

machine, with intercept provided by the Anima Gatherings (so, yes,
it IS a True Brujah Wall deck). Enkil Cog is pretty much a GW-insurance.
During the rounds, a few points were important:
- Powerbase Zurich would be an extremely nice addition.
- Summon History could be added (up to 3 copies)
- Perfect Paragon isn't as good as Tangle Atropo's Hand.

2012syasjc.author: Brett Schofield
2012syasjc.description:
A somewhat traditional "tap and cap" deck backed up with
the stealth offered by Vicissitude. I was pretty fortunate
in that I didn't face a real wall deck, and I was the only
political deck in the finals. But it is pretty ridiculous
how much pool this deck can acquire.

Crypt Selection: Velya and Lambach are the stars. Obviously
it is best for Velya to use Voter Cap, but refilling Lambach
for future Minion Taps is pretty good. I think there are a
couple of modifications that could be made to this deck.
More copies of Sascha Vykos (adv) could be added - she has
an amazingly good ability, but it is frustrating that she
can't use Mind of the Wilds for stealth. Sames goes for
Matteus, Flesh Sculptor (!Toreador) who could replace Meshenka.

Library: Over all, I was pleased with the amount of defense
(combat and bounce), stealth, and vote push this deck packs.
I only saw early crypt acceleration in one game, but it seems
hard to justify adding any more. On hind sight, I would
definitely drop the Crusade. I was surprised how often I
ended using Changeling to bleed.

2012motebny.author: Ira Fay
2012motebny.description:
Jay Kristoff has inspired previous decks of mine (http://thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2k7ctw1),
and this deck was also inspired by him, hence the name. You can read all about his deck here:

With some research from Mephistopheles, Jay outlined 6 design goals for his deck:
1) 9-12 different vampires without a star
2) Many pool generating cards
3) Cards that move vamps from crypt to uncontrolled
4) 60 cards
5) Doesn't appear frightening
6) Unusual

I started by thinking about what +2 Pool action I could take. It's hard to get that many Art Scams,
so I settled on Dark Mirror of the Mind. Then I had to figure out how to get a bunch of 8+ caps.
Eternals of Sirius was the best answer I could find, and it also solved #3 since I could use Mesu
Bedshet. I think I succeeded on all the design goals except #5, since it's really hard to convince
people that you're not frightening when you have 5 or more 8+ caps.

permanents into play quickly while not having to stack multiple

for 22 pool.

2011gc.description:
Description: Did some of the changes I talked
about after Arnheim last week. Ditched the Governs
for more Conditionig, which worked very well. Added
another Valerius ADV cause I expected S&B (I was wrong).
Added 1 Magic/ 1 IR Goggles, had no impact. Still played

some Flames of the Netherworld. Put in Smiling Jack, but
the deck is not blocky enough to defend it against more
than 1 player. Missed Chantry a whole lot this tourney,
might put it in instead of Jack. This deck could really
benefit from 2-3 Nose of the Hound to get rid of deflectors
before lunging, need to make room.

2011ano.author: John Bell
2011ano.description:
Description: I had a deck like this back in 2001, added Papillion
and Lilith's Blessing, hoping to keep blood on the minions.
The deck is very fast and almost guarantees that a table will not
time out. It's difficult to not make a target of yourself early,
especially if the First Traditions come up. The deck runs well
without them, but they keep the pool/minion count low enough to
ensure an advantage in most cases. The Justicar Retribution was
the all-star heads-up in the finals, burning Stanislava when
I had complete vote control.
2011ano.name: 1... 2... Skip a Few (turns)

2011ggs.description:
Description: This is some sort of Freak Show but I can not
stress enough that this is no one-turn deck. Ankara Citadel
first of course and then tool up with 5-10 actions each turn,
one of them being a bleed as big as possible that needs to
end up at prey's pool. The recursable Command the Legion
and Revelations makes this deck shine, everything else is
situational.
2011ggs.name: Glöggansiktet Gerald

2011bf2an0.description:

can only be played on the 2 6-caps. Maybe 3 Govern
7 Conditioning is the way to go. Also I wanted to play
4 Flames of the Netherworld (but didnt't have any) and
6 Apportation, so I settled for 3 Walk of Flame and
7 Apportation. WoF was used once in 4 games so should
be cut, and Apportation should be upped to 8-10. Powerbase:
Barranquilla should go, I'd like to include 1 more Magic
of the Smith and a IR Goggles. Always!!! get Heart of
Cheating as fast as possible.

2011nhhu.author: Asif Chaudhry
2011nhhu.description:
Description: After snatching defeat from the jaws of victory one
too many times while facing the Imbued, I decided I wanted to make
a deck that could effectively deal with them.
Thus, the inspiration for this deck.
Mordechai is the super star. Want to:
- burn allies (Mercy of Seth)
- block actions (built in +1 int, plus AUS)
- burn ash heap power/conviction cards (Trochomancy)
2011nhhu.name: Mordechai Ben Nun & Friends HATE THE IMBUED!

2011ecfcq0.author: Djordje Bjelajac
2011ecfcq0.description:
Original deck by Otso Saariluoma. Tweaked to handle a little bit more
intercept. I saw the idea on TWDA and since it featured two of my
favorite vampires I decided to try it out and loved the concept.
The concept is to get both Unmada and Scout Youngwood out, then recruit
your allies and call Parity Shifts and Reckless Agitations on your prey
to get him/her to Villein/tap or otherwise empty his/her vampires. Then
you start playing your shattering crescendos. Slow to start, but gets
stronger as the game progresses. I used to have another Dreams of the
Sphinx in the deck but it seems I put it in another deck since I use
this primarily for fun. It turned out well, since it would have just
contested on every table. I also noticed that in three of the four games
I played I managed to slow the Ashur decks considerably since I always
offered to play Ashurs after my opponents finished their first cycle if
they would also do the same. However, I only have one master phase and
six ashurs to start with and if the opponents stick to the deal it hurts
them in the long run.
2011ecfcq0.name: Nobody expects the Shattering Crescendo.

2011ffqjdfb.name: Mirror, mirror on the wall, exists someone that makes more pool than me?

2011ddlmno.description:

the "tap & cap" model - Villein, Papillon and Ashur's Tablets only
makes this better. The deck was conceived to punish many of the
wall-type decks, which are often in vogue around here. It's very
resilient, often difficult to oust, especially without having to
deal with Immortal Grapple.
2011ddlmno.name: Judgment Columbus: Blocking is Pain

2011spanishnat.author: Noel Giménez Infante
2011spanishnat.description:
Description: Este es el deck con el que pude ganar el nacional,
la verdad es que no me tocó ninguna mesa fácil y me tocó remar
muchísisisimo para llegar a la final. (Pico y piedra) Creo que
una de las claves de la final fue la mala elección de Ale sentándose
detrás mío con los Tupdogs, tuve que aguantar 16 visitas, pero
lo pude salvar. La verdad que excepto en la primera mesa, en todas
las demás me sobró el intercept, ya que me tocaron palos como panes
en toda y cada una de las partidas.
2011spanishnat.name: El sereto debe mantenerse

2011dbrdcag.description:
Zubeida leads the way, in his own Perfectionist manner, in righting the
wrongs done by those who are abusing the Public Trust. (Bleed, add
stealth, use the gained counter on an uncontrolled vampire, bring another
one into play that can do the same.) Frequently spent games with
2 vampires in torpor. Assembled in ~20 minutes the morning of the
tournament, it is missing the Freak Drives and Enticements and Wider
Views that surely could have made a difference in a few of the rounds.
Herbert Westin was nowhere to be found during the short time allowed
for assembly, so Robin Withers made it in instead.

2011fotmlac.description:

lunge with Misdirection, Pentex Subversion, Govern and Conditioning.

2011gatewaylac.author: Michael Courtois
2011gatewaylac.description:
Description: With the fragility of a combo deck such as this we decided
to make it smaller and utilize Luc, as opposed to fortitiude buddies, for
his handsize ability and Pentex removal with more Obfuscate, plus Sense The
Sin just invites Archon Investigation to further impede it's flow. Swalloweds
are decent combat defense (and offense if The Beast needs to visit somebody)
and Gramle gets the card you need right now. Also with the larger handsize
the inclusion of one Pentex seemed like a necessary evil, for another way to
deal with it or to just use it offensively.
2011gatewaylac.name: Nergal's a Beast

2011fitblac.author: David Litwin
2011fitblac.description:
This was a rehash of an older deck I had dismantled before KOT that I redesigned
with some newer cards and the hope that it played enough S:CE to survive Deep Song.
The deck never got to play a S:CE the entire tournament as every time it was in
combat it lacked one in hand, making me think it either needs 5-6 more or should
just remove all the No Trace and take your chances.

The crypt could also be tightened more to make the deck more consistent, I'd drop
everyone under 8 cap and play a few more copies of the Ventrue so I have more valid
targets for Zillah's Valley as multiple times I had 7 caps left over in my uncontrolled
region and no way to cycle a Zillah's Valley to burn the 5 pool. It would also
allow an inclusion of Ventrue Headquarters/Ephor with a significantly higher chance of
being able to put it into play.
2011fitblac.name: Dirty Sinks

2011bos4bp.author: Marcin Watras
2011bos4bp.description:
Description: Deck based on Johannes Walch's Brujah Debate deck
he played during WoN in June. I added 3 cards to the original deck -
Jake, Carlton and Aranthebes. I would add Dreams of the Sphinx
instead of Cryptic Rider. Aranthebes wasn't useful but it would
help to contest it with my prey if he had played one.

This deck has some potencial, but in case your pred/prey is playing
a deck with fast setup if is very difficult to get VP's. If mid game
you should have 15+ pool and several minions striking for 3+. Smiling
Jack is a good option for late game when playing against two players.
Brujah Debate deck is very strong when played agains unexperienced
player who had never pleayed agains it before and there are lots of
them as Brujah Debate decks are not so common these days.

I will play that deck during a bigger tournament in the future.
2011bos4bp.name: Brujah Debate 60 cards

2011NACd20.author: Matthew Morgan
2011NACd20.description:
Description: It's rush combat with a strong master module. Master cards
are the best in the game. I'd always rather have too many than too few.
The name is because the final was won 2-1-1-1 and Fish and Stick lead the
way while Nana stayed hidden in my crypt. Fish is only in the deck to make
it count as a Guruhi deck for TWDA purposes.

One might wonder why only 4 Nana when she's the star? The answer is that
it's way better to have no Nana than all Nana. This deck needs a bunch of
minion actions to succeed

I really liked having AI here in the final, though I wound up not
playing it. Mbare Market probably isn't worth the slot. Should be a
2nd Fame, I think. Otherwise the masters worked out very well.

The Entrancement and Well-Marked didn't really earn their keep at any
point, though Well-Marked is typically a free action at least. I play
fewer Deep Songs than Martin's version because I'm not trying to rush
with every minion with every action. I bleed for 1 a little or stay up.
I want my prey to go forward. I don't want to simply squish him. Coming
out of the gate too fast is a mistake.

Very few reactions. Sense the Savage Way should probably go since only
Nana can play them. I had multiple situations where I would have liked to
block with somebody else but couldn't because of the restriction on that
card. Getting to 2 intercept is nice, but it isn't worth the cost.

Very consistent. Not a lot can survive repeated hits from this. Of course
it's not fun to run into other ANI decks, but them's the breaks.
2011NACd20.name: Salmon Fishstick

2011wontd0.description:
Description: (Imbued Chainsaw Rush)

A couple of years ago, John stitched the Chainsaw rush into
a Dancing Imbued deck and the two of us tuned the deck into
the current state over a couple of months.

It is a bit more fragile than some of the intermediate builds
but is consistent. I considered adding Veil of Darkness and
the Rising, but opted to leave them out for this run.

My favorite moment of the tourament win with this deck was
bleeding with the Vagabound Mystic, who had successfully
equipped a Laptop Computer, IR Goggles, Leather Jacket and
the Heart of Nizchetus.
2011wontd0.name: Balls of Stihl

2011wp19bp.description:

2011zban.author: Izaak Havelaar
2011zban.description:
Description: Ever since cards like Reunion Kamut and Art of Memory
were printed, I have been wanting to build a deck with all these
Black Hand toys. I recently traded for enough Seraph's Seconds to
build a competitive Black Hand deck and try and get the most out
of them. I experimented with !Tremere and Lasombra for a bit at
first, before ending up with Assamites. Of course it should have
been obvious all along Assamites are the best pick for such a deck,
since they are the only clan that has two Seraphs in the same
grouping and get five different Black Hand crypt cards in that
same grouping.

This deck is a bloat/multiact deck at its core and, but with so
many actions a turn, it allows you keep pressure on your prey while
still bloating enough to survive even the most aggressive bleed
predators. It's especially important to build up a solid ready
region with at least a Seraph with a Tattoo Signal plus two other
vampires before you start throwing multiple Losses a turn at your
prey. Once the Watchtower comes into play even the most dedicated
wall decks will have trouble blocking every critical action and
you can oust everyone at your leisure.

It seems master-heavy at first, but with 6 trifles and four copies
of Information Highway it works out just fine. There should probably
go an Archon Investigation in there instead of one of the Info Highways
or maybe the Yoruba Shrine. The three Ashur Tablets are kinda critical
as well, because in every game I played with this deck, I ran out of
cards in the endgame. If one gets cancelled it's not a big deal, because
you can just retrieve it with the Sargon Fragment.

Fourth Cycle is in there to make sure the Watchtower's upkeep stays
at one pool per turn when other people play Unmasking or Anthelios.
As a bonus it also gets rid of them. In the end I never needed it,
but I still think it's a good idea.

This section is perfect. I always had a Loss when I needed one and
in every game I played so far I have managed to bring out 4 or 5 different
minions. Reunion Kamut is really good, especially since it works on older
vampires as well.

It's mostly there so I can retrieve a cancelled Ashur Tablet, but
it's also quite handy to recycle a Loss or a Haqim's Law. I should
probably add a single copy of Trochomancy to the deck to mess with
Ashur/Liquidation based decks.

Art of Memory is amazing. I used them to recycle an Elder Impersonation
to oust a particularly troublesome Henry Taylor twister deck, I used them
to recycle Haqim's Laws to stay alive against a !Ventrue bleeder without
a predator and I used them to get lot of mileage out of a single copy of
Loss. On top of it, you get to flush an unwanted card (say, extra
Information Highways or Gehenna Events) out of your hand. If I were
to play it again, I'd swap a Seraph's Second for a fifth Art of Memory.
2011zban.name: Pancake Mix

2011tottco.author: David Wilson
2011tottco.description:
Description: The deck was a lot of fun, but it really needed
a lot of cycling. The Recure the Homeland was the all start
with Burst of Sunlight and Target Vitals, it really did lots
of damage. The trick of this deck is to tool up while bounding
bleeds forwards and backwards around the table, the My Enemies
Enemy are quite intentional, as this deck doesn't go forward
too hard, which means my prey gets going, taking table pressure
off my grand predator, I try to fix that here. The allies and
Terrell Harding (wider view needs to be here) suck some blood off
as a means to stop Deflections when you do lunge forward.
In round one after having 2 allies burned and my first vampire
with a Vessel, Blood Doll, Ivory Bow and Rutor's Hand on turn 4,
I managed to lunge for 12 undeflected 4 turns later with the
Heidelberg, all the time just bouncing and tweaking blood off
vampires. Society of Leopold takes a very close 2nd to all
star card, it really allowed me to stop other methheads as
needed. This deck was something I tooled with on JOL, it
never did well and I rebuilt it the morning of the event,
it does have flow problems, so note if you play it, you will
be discarding every turn if you want a chance in hell. Truth
be told, my win came from luck, and my ability to capitalize
on it. The last bit of advice, ditch the harvest rites, trust
me, they suck here. Thanks to Jay for getting such a large
showing from Columbus and to the Newark crew for making it out!

2011lvctmorning.author: David Litwin
2011lvctmorning.description:
The deck plays generally the same as any stealth/vote deck with a more
interesting stealth module. Ideally Armin Brenner is your first
minion and should always be first unless he isn't in your opening
crypt. He is the only minion in the crypt that can maximize the use
of all cards in the crypt and his 1 pool/vote adds up over the course
of the game. The deck will play quite a few cards each turn and
maximizing cards like Forced March for stealth and untap is key.

The deck can generally bloat fast enough to handle a moderately fast
bleeding predator and Majesty or Resist Earth's Grasp will slow down
Animalism rush significantly while accepting that a Grappling foe will
kill the deck. Undele is key for late game antics to make sure your
two other actions/turn are exactly what you want them to be.

While it never showed, gaining potentially 5 pool calling a Black
Forest Base action is rather nice. The changes I would make after
playing it outside of the local playgroup would be two fewer KRCs and
another Neonate Breach and then some other damage vote or maybe even
a utility vote like Snipe Hunt/Permanent Vacation to take out late
threats that can be brought back. Delaying Tactics recycled in the
finals against me slowed down my offense several turns.

2011sabotuk.author: Dave Knowles
2011sabotuk.description:
Thanks to #vtes on SorceryNet for critiqueing this
deck a million times for me, and Hugh & John for
putting up with oddball ideas when I should be
playing something more sensible.

Beatrice is *golden*. Leech, burn the Second Sight when
announced, untap, bleed with pot options that worry people.
I'm tempted to have an extra one. Keith and Esoara have never
seen play.

Seems to flow just about right, maybe needs another Intercept location.

Veil of Darkness kills tables. Everyone will hate you
for it (and with good reason), but it's pretty much a key
card to drop via Fortschritt if necessary. It saves me
repeatedly, including killing the Stealth on the Ancilla
Empowerment that would have killed me in the final.

Probably needs 1-2 more Actions, no idea what to lose to manage it, though.

I have no idea why the more common Nephandus deck runs 10.
I never see 10, I never can afford 10, and I run out of turns
before I'd get 10. Young Bloods and Carlton can also Leech.

Once again, a smidge too light, really.

The kicker. Nobody expects a Nephandus to Disarm you,
and nobody expects a Nephandus to survive a Torn Signpost
*and* Disarm you.

2011gatlno.author: John Bell
2011gatlno.description:
Description: The deck is so named because every game I have played it, someone at the table
has commented that I would have to run out of Faerie Wards at some point. Until
it's seen in action, it is hard to describe just how effective a wall this deck
can be without blocking at all. The deck is extremely slow, but relies on
locking down its predator to get itself entrenched. Eternal Vigilance really
makes the deck obnoxious - it does require you to block, but judicious usage can
truly sap your predator's will - attempt to block a hunt or vote without
intercept or ensure that you have an Obedience in hand for 0-stealth actions.
The Rack and Papillion for Marconius assure that you can Faerie Wards to your
heart's content and Smiling Jack to end games. The major challenge for the deck
is increasing Marconius' capacity to ensure everyone is a legal target for
Faerie Wards/Banishment.

Both actions are just awesome for the deck. Depending on the table, I used
Goblinism to either get Papillion or Secure Haven most often. There should also
probably be some Govern's in this deck to utilize all the wonderful superior
Dominate, but for some reason that always scares people.

Mylan can either bleed or be another way to keep the Marconius-machine
untapped and running. The other two are there to try and ensure that my prey is
losing maximum pool to Smiling Jack in the endgame, but can also be helpful
keeping a predator in a hunt-loop.

Always nice for a deck that likes to sit around and wait for opportunities.

Huge against breeder decks and other weenies.

Virtually ensures I will never run out of Faerie Wards, offers pool gain,
and the ability to retrieve early discards - can't say enough good about them.

Most recent addition to the deck in an attempt to keep my prey from running
away from me; excellent synergy with making Marconius older anyway and often
times this deck just happens to be the political power at a table.

To test whether this card was worth playing, I wanted to ensure I always had
a few in hand. It might be a bit much, but the card is so very good when only
paying 1 blood. It is also nice to be able to play it at basic [myt] on a
bounced bleed to keep the pressure on my predator.

Probably should include a few Deflections in the deck, but the idea was to
really try and abuse Faerie Wards. I may try to drop 2-3 in the future and
replace them with Deflection.
2011gatlno.name: He Has To Run Out Sometime...

2011wtano0.author: John Bell
2011wtano0.description:
Probably one of more vicious and aggressive decks I have built.
The idea is denying opponents key resources in the form of their
Masters. The obvious choices are prey's pool gain and predator's
offensive cards, but it becomes more difficult to decide what
permanents to allow in play across table. The stealth-bleed module
works quite well without a single master, but the deck funcitons
under the assumption that many decks are crippled without their
master phases.The deck physically can not bleed for greater than
3, which means I have no worries for Archon Investigation and
bounce isn't as crippling as when a bleed of 6 is redirected.
The pool generation in the deck mostly comes from Kindred Spirits,
ousting my prey, or The Call in a pinch.

2011auolac.name: Junta

2011tlfno0.author: John Bell
2011tlfno0.description:
Description: Most of the decks I've seen with the Ishtarri
revolve around Ayo and voting, I wanted to go a different
angle with this deck. The original concept was to have multiple
informants out so that I could have an idea of what everyone
held in their hand. It was built as a combat/wall deck and
spends a lot of time sitting around trying to build up.
The No Secrets can often get burned, but isn't a disaster
since there are more to be had.

Should remove Shasa and Honorine for 2x Ayo Igoli,
I didn't want to invest that much into a single minion
with this deck, but she's really good for it.

Enchants should be changed to Entrancement

I would consider dropping the hunting ground for Carlton van Wyk, who should have been in here to start with.

Both Wakes should be changed for On the Qui Vive which would allow me to throw a Procurer in the way of a rush-action.
2011tlfno0.name: Ishtarri No Ayo

2011tbassbi.author: Alessandro Donati
2011tbassbi.description: Description: New Ahrimanes Wall Deck with Anarch Tricks.
2011tbassbi.name: Ahrimane Protectorate

2011trmsf0.author: Christian Nislev
2011trmsf0.description:
Description: The classic Henry Taylor-twister deck where Henry ends up
blocking everything and ousting with Smiling Jack. I felt the deck was
a bit too passive, so added Clan Impersonation and Madness Network
which allows for some serious end game bleed punch with Anima
Gathering and Earth Control stealth. Bleeding at the end of your
predator's turn gives you the edge and a pool which pays for Jack. 31
cards is too much, but there's some nifty mechanics that adds
flexibility to the classic deck.
2011trmsf0.name: A Twist of Madness

2011pstf55.author: Otso Saariluoma
2011pstf55.description:
Osebo intercept/combat with Andre added as an opportunistic
ousting mechanism. In order to get GWs, this deck needs
quite a few turns, so one or two players should be
eliminated quickly; don't hesitate to rush cross-table
and/or backoust to bring the table down to three players
as fast as possible.
2011pstf55.name: Anger Management

2011qcfvvf.author: Jérôme Bauzon
2011qcfvvf.event: French NCQ - Rencontre hivernale à St Henri
2011qcfvvf.name: DI Why ?

2011nrqtwri.author: Randal Rudstam
2011nrqtwri.description:
and Isak Esbjörnsson Bjärmark/Adam Esbjornsson (almost stolen even)
Description: Yea so shit loads of cred to Erik, Isak, Adam and Alex.
Girls will find inner peace with minor modifications. House of Sorrow
and coven generated 4 extra blood in the final which was very nice.
Thanks for a great tournament!! God bless America ;)

with some changes in the crypt (added 4 Tupdogs)

2011dmno.author: John Bell
2011dmno.description:
Description: A breed-and-boon deck which revolves around Guruhi Are
the Land: a free, versatile card which can provide situational untap,
extra blood when hunting, or +bleed. Dream World was ridiculously good,
but in two games getting No Secrets with the Kevlar Vest was the
game-breaker. For a future build, I would be tempted to include more
vests and No Secrets after the success it brought me, but the original
intent was for that to be a side feature of the deck.
2011dmno.name: We Are the Land

2011gnc2k10.author: Emiliano Imeroni
2011gnc2k10.description:
Description: Maris Streck and Lutz von Hohenzollern
go the Derange/Dementia/assorted nastiness way
2011gnc2k10.name: Marilutz

2011sorno0.author: John Bell
2011sorno0.description:
Description: Cybele's master phases are key to working the
Tend the Flocks for either speed or pool generation.
The Ashur Tablets give me freedom to move cards quickly
while allowing me to retrieve them for later when I need
to tune my hand. The idea is to be able to have permanent
+bleed on as many minions as possible, lay as low as possible
and bloat to live.
2011sorno0.name: What the Flock?!

2010fs2ii0.author: John Bell
2010fs2ii0.description:
An experiment with Touch of Pain: the idea being that late
game it is as good as a rush or better - leaving my actions
open to other options.
2010fs2ii0.name: To the Death! No! To the Pain.

2010tjindar.author: Ivan Marin-Rivas
2010tjindar.description:
Description: First combat is to cycle in to necessary cards, both in
graveyard and in hand. After that play Ashurs and recycle the necessary
cards back into library and deck. Always keep in mind the amount of
ashurs in the deck so that you don't choke on masters.

Soulscan for Agaitas if needed for added flavor and utility.
2010tjindar.name: Der Räuber und der Prinz

2010fsss.author: Tomas Wallmur
2010fsss.description:
A light bleed/block deck with free vampires and Henry and Aksinya for
defense.
2010fsss.name: Henry's Influence

2010aamsjc.author: Mike Zajac
2010aamsjc.description:
Vote and bleed down prey, and reassign pool via Parity Shifts to keep
others from being ousted; bounce with Deflections and reduce combat
with Obedience and Read Intentions; slow to start up and weak against
Grapples and heavy combat, but tends to keep things interesting, as
passing votes is rarely a problem.
2010aamsjc.name: Obey Redux

2010fssjc0.author: Joel Marbella
2010fssjc0.description: Description: Standard Bruise and Bleed deck.
2010fssjc0.name: The Iggy & Laz Tag Team (with Groupies!)

2010fscolumbus.author: John Bell
2010fscolumbus.description:
Description: This deck is definitely more along the "toolbox" style
than prefer to run but I wanted to try something a little different.
The two votes are there mainly for vote protection, but can also allow
me to play Eternal Vigilance if the stars properly align. The
Pandora's Whispers often help fine tune a hand, I may consider adding
more although I'm not sure what I'd drop.
2010fscolumbus.name: Fairies Wear Boots

2010psnnshf.author: Simon Reed
2010psnnshf.description:
Kind of a toolbox combat deck. Mostly this ends up being constant
nibbling at your prey each turn and picking off soft targets with the
Garou.
2010psnnshf.event: Praxis Seizure: New New Super Heavy Funk
2010psnnshf.name: Anarch Garou

2010fscoimbra.author: Tiago Brum
2010fscoimbra.description:
Description: After the EC in 2009 I thought about the decks that
impressed me the most and Hugh's Gentlemen with Sticks was one of
them. At the time Grinders weren't all that known in Portugal.
Being the fan of Ventrue that I am, I thought the KoT vampires would
bring advantages that the Sabbat vampires don't have, like 2nd
Tradition, inherent votes for defense and other goodies.
Played with deck in tournaments for a year and went to every Final
with it. Except the EC:(
2010fscoimbra.name: Better Gentlemen, Same Sticks

2010boogalooii.author: Simon Reed
2010boogalooii.event: Boogaloo II: Revenge of the Boogaloo
2010boogalooii.name: My AAA

2010fsbillerica.author: Kevin Mullen
2010fsbillerica.description:
The deck is straight forward offense. The only action in the deck that
doesn't have any offensive potential is Carlton Van Wyck which I threw
in last minute. Get out 2 vampires and try to bleed, vote and recruit
with them each turn. The first action is usually the most important
and has the Uncontrolled Impulse to push it through. Majesty and
change of target gets through and defenders until you can get your
actions through. Decent pool gain to slow down your predator. If you
are in a really bad spot, bloat and vote upstream. Don't bother
leaving any vampires for blocking unless you don't have any actions
left, or you are looking at static intercept combat with no modifiers
to push your actions through.
2010fsbillerica.name: All You Need Is Oust

2010fsbny0.author: James Wilhelm

2010hunrb0.author: Martin Major
2010hunrb0.description:
Fast and aggressive rush combat. Make 1st vp asap and decide who to
stay 1 on 1 with. Follow the basic combat doctrine to backrush first
and then play without a predator.

/could need more copies of Animalism skill card. Fear of Mekhet was a
metagame choice and burned a Legendary Unmada. Wider View never showed
up when needed. Frontal Assault is pure gold!/

/my version is really not about blocking. Random intercept is good to
keep people guessing and blocking deflected bleeds/

/very solid combat package, Target Vitals and Terror Frenzy are
extremely useful/

/discarded when drawn to early and taken back into hand after a
completed Ashur Cycle in the midgame. Awesome bonus to your ousting power/

2010nacd20.description:
The main strategy of the deck is to get the best use out of
Hannibal(A)'s untap ability to act twice on my own turn, then be able
to untap later for defense if needed. There is a clear vote strategy
in the deck, but I also put in a good amount of toolbox.

2010lcqnol.author: Mark Loughman
2010lcqnol.description:
Description: Credit where credit is due. I had built a Chamelon module
into a Ayo-Anarch deck a while back, and as such was familiar with the
mechanics of it, but Matt Wedge took it to a new level. He proposed a
mono-Snake deck accelerated by Eternals of Sirius. I've spent the last
8 months learning to build and play 60 card decks, more in the style of
Jay. I went Group 4 for this, because Nakhthorheb's inherent multi-acting
is so strong. Thanks also to Darby for some tweaks in the Master mix. I
would probably delete one of the support snakes in favor of a second
Cagliostro... Synergy between him and Nak is huge.

wants a couple more On the Qui Vive (instead of a couple Wakes) and

bleed actions via Tryphosa, allows you to have less stealth cards and
more space for heavy defense module. It allows you to block your preys
poolgaining actions and tapping him out in the process. So bleeding
and gaining pool via bleeding is teh way to win. Deck has a hard time
to sweep, but stays alive long enough to make the table.

2010finnishecq.description:
Description: The same deck I played before, this time with slight
alterations, as I found Unmada too important to miss in the opening
crypt. Temptation of Greater Power was actually an excellent addition.
If you want to use the combo in every single game (which I didn't),

2010kaldecq.description:
Description: Classic Triple A concept enhanced with the new big A, Ashur Tablets.

The only change I would make in this deck is to add an Anarchist Uprising
and an Archon (look, more A's!) and cut out a Perpetual Care and a Psyche.
I had not realized Alastor doesn't allow you to rush allies and that was
mighty annoying in two of the four games.

The two cards that got my the win today were Metro Underground (having
an untapped Assault Rifle is *huge*) and the Entrancement, that I could
play unblockable in the finals to steal a Nephandus, bring it back to
my hand with Ashur's the next turn and steal another Nephandus.

2010pwbla4.author: Michael Courtois
2010pwbla4.description:
Description: The deck SHOULD have a Heart of Cheating but it was in
another deck and I forgot to add it before the tourney. Mistress must
get a Rutor's Hand first thing, then Alastor, then Helicopter, then
Magic the Ankara Citadel. From there, there is enough in the deck to go in

Orlando is always your second minion to help grab the political reins at
the table. If all goes well, you'll be the last one standing.
2010pwbla4.name: Mistress Fanchion doesn't have a Heart!

2010pwbla3.author: Robert Scythe
2010pwbla3.description:
Description: Infernal Pursuits, Aura Readings and the Barrens to get
your guns on, Ashurs to get back all those necessary discards. In the
tournament I drew the Barrens in my opening hand all three games, too
good. All the Forceds would be Eyes if I owned that many, though I did
use a Forced on a Mind Raped, Pulsed Kallista with only one blood to
fail a block. There's usually another Quicken, 2 DI's and another
intercept location (really missed the DI's). This really wants at
least 1 Aire even if Marcellus cannot use it, and he needs to be the
main. Rather have a Jake than the Hunting Grounds.
2010pwbla3.name: The Quick and the Dead

2010norwegianecq.author: Patrick Robinsson
2010norwegianecq.description: Description: Almost as created and played by Forrest Hyppa April 2009
2010norwegianecq.name: Brutal politics

have to find another abuse for Art of Memory.
2010pwblaQ.name: Cholinesterase Inhibition - Last Call

2010pwbla1.author: Darby Keeney
2010pwbla1.description:
Comments: Many thanks to Fred Scott for lending me 2 Tupdogs for this
tournament. Generally, I have found a 2.5:1 Tupdog-to-!Tremere ratio
to work out pretty well, though a long string of Dogs at the top pf
one's crypt is frustrating.

The objective for this deck is to get additional mileage from the
Tupdogs... decreasing their effective cost from 1 pool per action to
0.5 pool per action and further leveraging both the rush and the slave
option (rush first, untap, available for slave clause, take an action
of the slave clause is not needed).

The deck is supposed to carry 1 more Ashur Tablet, but I seem to own
only 5 at this time. 4, 6 or 7 seem like the right numbers to me,
depending on your risk tolerance and recycling needs.

Synergies:
Carver's + Dragonbound and Carver's + Vessel are pretty clear.
Carver's + Raw Recruit is an indefinate hold on a Recruit target (that
could not be Graverobbed). Carver's not affecting Tupdogs is a bonus.

Heidleburg can save master vampires from dangerous hunting
requirements, can empty a Tupdog of before it explodes and allows 2
Hand of Conrad actions per turn.

A "good" combat ran "set close and agg hands, Grapple, prevent and
untap".
2010pwbla1.name: [2010 TW] The World's Biggest Small Multirushers

2010breakthecodess.author: Caroline Hyll
2010breakthecodess.description:
Description: A rather classic Lasombra bloat deck. During the final my
predator played Anthelios in mid-game, which was wonderful with my
three master phase actions. Perhaps it should be added to the deck.
2010breakthecodess.name: Francisco wanted to be a papa

2010motenyc.author: Ruben Feldman
2010motenyc.description:
Description: Bring out little Ravnos, who in turn bring out littler
Ravnos. Cycle Mozambique Allures easily by going Laibon and the
calling votes using Eldest are Kholo. Vote defense is also Eldest are
KHOLO!

A few comments on the deck:
Turns out the events were mostly useless, destroying my handsize. The
only time someone played the Uncoiling, I was glad to see it!
First time i try heart of Nizchetus: disapointing, i would have
prefered a Tarot or another trinket...
Archon Investigation was, once again, completely useless - being a
dead card for all the time i ever had it in hand.
Probably too many things going on in this deck, jammed a lot. Need to
cut down to 60-66 cards, notably the events, some masters and still
not convinced about the Eldest are Kholo vote mechanism...
2010motenyc.name: Eldest are Ravnos

2010pshilversum.description:

I never needed Anarch Railroad, but the Free Press came in handy
quite a few times. I was considering to drop the Blood Dolls
altogether and in retrospect I should have. An extra Dreams and a few
Washes or Suddens would have helped greatly.

The Dutch meta has been loaded with allies for a while so I figured
Entrancement would be a safe bet. As it turned out, I didn't see a
single ally and mostly discarded them. 23 Undue Influence was a tad
bit too high. Should go down to 19 or 20.

This worked perfectly for me. My Enemy's Enemy was intended more as
intercept than as bounce and it did its job perfectly. Two or so more
wakes wouldn't be bad though, as I usually had to fully tap out

2010nerqwri.author: John Eno
2010nerqwri.description:
This is my attempt to make a Ventrue version of the !Ventrue
intercept/combat deck I've been playing, because the new law firm has
such an excellent crypt. Most of the card choices here seem pretty
obvious, but I'll attempt some Morganesque deck commentary for those
that might seem odd or should be changed.

In theory, Mary Anne Blaire is great for this deck. In practice, I think she's
probably too big and should be changed into another Graham and a
smaller vampire. Emily Carson would be a good choice.

I really want his card to be good, and this would seem to be the
deck for it to shine. I don't think I've ever actually played it in
the year or so that I've been working on this deck, though, so that's
probably a pretty good sign that it could be usefully replaced.

Absolutely no idea why there isn't a Giant's Blood in here,
particularly since I put that card into just about every deck I make.
The Island will definitely be changed out for one in the future.

The idea here was that using Scouting Mission over more Governs
would save me blood. In practice, they should all be Governs.

This needs more bleed punch, and the free cards can probably be
safely changed into Conditioning without worrying about its blood
cost. During the tournament, I kept wondering why I was drawing so few
bleed modifiers. More evidence that you should be very familiar with a
deck before you play it in a rated event...

Too much damage prevention. During all four games of the tournament,
there were times when I found myself looking at three or four combat
cards and wishing that they were anything else. Matthew Hirsch took a
great picture of my hand during round three, in which you see six
damage prevention cards and a Walking Stick. Ouch. Some of this will
be taken out for more bleed mods.

If Mary Anne doesn't appear in the crypt any more, this card
obviously needs to be changed into a Sport Bike.

I still haven't figured out if Palatial Estate is ever worth the
action or card slot. I think math is against me on this one, but I'll
leave it here until I can decide definitively.

People will probably mock me for the Shotguns again, but they've
never done wrong by me.

Another "in theory this is great" card, particularly for lockdown
during the two-player game. Probably one or both should be more
straightforward offensive votes like Anarchist Uprising or KRC.

Enough wake tech to make Peal grumpy during the finals when he was
trying to oust me, so it must be just the right amount.
2010nerqwri.name: Lawyers, Guns and Money

2010ftwri0.author: Jesse Cross-Nickerson
2010ftwri0.description:
A fairly self-explanatory crypt. My primary concern was to get POT on everybody
so that they can fling superior gates. Calebros is the one exception, but he is
well worth it for ANI and a prince title.

I've never been able to tap SchreckNET, but it's an easy action to cycle.
Some day, I'll probably get to use it.

These are often very useful as stealth for early game set up actions,
especially Casino's 0 stealth action to move blood. Given how often I
use them at basic, it might be wise to swap a couple for Lost in Crowds.

The beauty of this combat package is its consistency, coupled with the ability
to surprisingly divert from the playbook. I have been able to shut down some
very nasty combat decks simply by always having a gate to manuever and do some
damage, and then by surprisingly ending combat or dodging (there used to be some
Behind You, and it could go back in) when I got caught in a bind. Flesh Bond
is great for its flexibility, as it deals 3R damage with Casino's special.

These tend to go on the support minions, not on Casino. They really help
get the oust in once I've crippled my prey's minions

A previous version of this deck, which got me to a final at Origins,
spent a total of 0 pool on library card costs. I added a Pentex Subversion
because it is awesome, and to contest should one land on Casino. (I would
still prefer that it be banned.) Spending so little pool is a major part
of what makes this deck work. Casino and Nikolaus both help get Nosferatu
at reduced prices, and I never bring out more than 4 vampires. Usually I
stick with 3, or even 2 under severe pressure. I use the extra pool as a
buffer because at some point in the game I need to tap out against my prey,
and then wake several times to stop her recovery actions. A lot of wall deck
players seem to imagine that they can do this and magically cycle into the
right mix of combat and reactions. Usually that won't happen. However, by
keeping my pool as high as possible, I can afford to take some serious hits
from my predator while I turn my defense into offense.

I would certainly entertain the possibility of cutting some STSW
for more 2nd Traditions.
2010ftwri0.name: Facebook Stalker

2k9sixthtradbc.description:
Desk: Beasts on the plains, twirling their canes
Description: This desk is inspired by Hugh Angseesing's
deck (and others) of similar name. I wanted to see if I
could make the Fortitude combat + WWS work for Akunanse.
Since the bleed offense is obviously weaker without dom,
and because I wanted to use Freak Drive and have 2 useful
actions for each minion, I added votes, which worked
pretty well. No Secrets is strong, but I was afraid of
Pentex, so I wanted to play a deck that had a reasonable
chance of getting out 2 Magaji. Also, using the Matt
Morgan school of thought, I wanted to have some good
non-threatening building actions early-game, while my prey
weakens my grand-prey. Wise Spider and Owl Companion are
great for that. This deck has limited untaps, but
canceling bounces with Terra Incognita requires only one
untapped minion, which was pretty easy given Wise Spider

2k9lobotomypa.author: Jessie Ellison
2k9lobotomypa.description:
Description: The idea behind this deck is of course primarily stealth
bleed, with a secondary function of trying to choose one's battles.
Chanjelin Ward and Redcap Wilder pose undesirable consequences to other
Methuselah's vampires, while Shadow Twin and Riddle Phantastique
effectively single out targets and attempt to make them weaker. With
the powerful combat supplied by Mytherceria and Obtenebration, these
vampires can usually choose whether they want to strike hard or make a
quick getaway. Archon Investigations were added to dissuade others
from trying big bleeds, and Centralized Background Checks to make the
dreaded Poker a little more expensive to get out. The strongest
vampire in this deck is, arguably, Marconius since he is the only one
to possess all three disciplines at superior as well as paying 1 less
blood for Mytherceria cards, but this deck really does not focus on
any one vampire in particular. Rather it focuses on getting as many
vampires out as possible, starting out rather slowly to create a wall
of Faerie mischief late in the game.

and 3 Vitals). After playing some friendly games and
this tournament I will replace two cards for another
cats guidance and on the qui vive. Otherwise I am
happy with all my choices.

cool for me. With some luck I made 4vp in final

don't want to enter. Just wait the game out and take the last two VPs

against vote decks with stealth - but thankfully I never had to face

2k9origins4.author: Hugh Angseesing
2k9origins4.description:
This was the only deck I could really put together for Ebony Kingdom
as I didn't have very many EK cards yet. It was meant to have 4
Quicken Sight, but I guess I accidentally put in an extra. 5 is too
many. The 5th should be Enhanced Senses or something. Also, some of
the cards in the deck (like Familial Bond) are junk, but I wanted to
try everything new. It was originally intended to have Aye, but they
didn't make the cut.

I played this untested in the US Championship and had a very
Goldilocks experience. The first table was too stealthy and I jammed
on combat. The second one was too fighty and I couldn't keep out of
torpor. The third table was just right and I won easily. Hugh
borrowed the deck for the Sunday tournament and made the final where
he won basically by being in the best shape after the table collapsed
(a fine way to win).

His only comment to me was the deck could use a couple of Camera
Phones. Probably a good plan.

Powerbase: Luanda is quite good. It's maybe the only thing here that
makes this deck something other than a poor Toreador gun deck without
the bleed potential.
2k9origins4.name: It's Pronounced "HUG-huh"

2k9acclcq0.author: Simon Reed
2k9acclcq0.description:
Deck: I love the Tremere
This deck is all about being flexible and tooling up with whatever the
game situation dictates. Constant pressure forward and bring out the
hordes of Tremere to overwhelm. Seems to work pretty well most of the
time, could maybe do with another Muaziz for her extra stealth for
forward motion but her disciplines aren't great.

Deck based on concepts I saw from Barnaby Dromgool and refined using
Steve Harris' deck from last years LCQ in Melbourne.
2k9acclcq0.name: Unknown

2k9marseillemq.name: Mais où vas-tu, mon gros Lulu ?

2k9belgianecq.author: Sebastian Meurer
2k9belgianecq.description:
Description: The deck is a Nosferatu multi-action toolbox with an
emphasis on bleeding. The foundation of the deck is Cock Robin's
special ability to untap after a successful action requiring
Animalism. Also Baron Dieudonne can untap after a successful action
(but only by paying a blood). Another untap possibility is provided by
Warsaw Station. With Tier of Souls, Deep Song and eventually Enkil Cog
the deck has considerable bleed potential. Thanks to Preternatural
Strength you only need to make room for few extra combat cards to be
very effective in combat, while being able to do "defensive rushing"
with Deep Song.
Maybe the deck's biggest advantage in a tournament is that other
players tend to underestimate its bleed potential and in general have
trouble assessing the deck's capabilities.
2k9belgianecq.name: Cogwork Brussels

3 with your IC's. A sprinkling of combat and bounce. Suffers vs
dedicated combat or walls. Should probably include a DI just for things
like No Secrets. The Force of Personalities are mostly for allies,
although doubles as more SCE. I only use the Aire with a non-IC, I'm
very Archon Investigation averse... Ashurs are gold, and definitely won
me the final, and probably helped me win at least one other game.

While others play complicated decks, whine alot and try to make weird

Julius dental care" deck and switched Potence for Animalism (Gate for
Aid, Increased for Crows). I can only wonder how good the deck should
have been if I actually owned 14 Deep Song.

2k9glrqco0.description:

Eyes of Argus is _SO_ efficient for this scheme that I was
able to slide in a touch more combat (Rego Mortus). I also
went to 4 Smiling Jacks. A first turn Jack means I don't have
to worry about a time out at the table. Ponticulus is also very cool.
2k9glrqco0.name: Traditional Princess

2k9ncbgfnd.description:

consistent +2 stealth on votes. Combat is mainly deterrence combat.
The deck can also bleed heavy when it plays its New Carthage.

2k9nfeqparis.name: 2 bad broken guys

2k9thevics.author: Jason Ryan
2k9thevics.description:
Description: Very reslient deck, but not really capable of fast ousts.
Need to do something to speed it up. Giant's Blood was gold all day.
Obediences were gold. Sniper Rifles were useless in ANI heavy meta.
Ashur Tablets weren't great either - if I got them up early, I didn't
really need to recur anything, and if I got them late, the game was
already over. Would be better off replacing them with some funk
(Millicent, From a Sinking Ship, etc).

Anthelios + 3MPA's = Joyyyyyyy
2k9thevics.name: The Beautiful People

2k9ecminiqsabadell.author: Iñaki Puigdollers
2k9ecminiqsabadell.description:
Builder and Player: Iñaki Puigdollers, inspired by "Sudario Diary"
Orian Gissler' s deck

Note: most people ask why do I play Tupdog here, there are plenty of
reasons indeed: permits me not to repeat vampires which grants better
crypt cycling, once on table they can recruit a generic ally (w/o fear
of being blocked and sent to torpor) before vanishing, they give you
specific rush defense, may play delaying tactics, and in the ash-heap
they may turn into wraiths once KD is full... though it' s a pity
they are non-unique.

After the Tournament I would only add a Vox Domini, maybe instead of
Giant' s Blood
2k9ecminiqsabadell.name: "Tupdog's Diary"

2k9alastorsvilleins.author: Antti Tirilä
2k9alastorsvilleins.description:
Description: Radoslaw Staszewski's recent deck from the news group.
Little tweaks here and there, especially taking more out of Jacob's
special. I never used Frontal Assault but it has potential. Loki's
Gifts fit nicely here as you'll be hunting after Tribute. The deck can
bleed pretty well but Fame and Dragonbound were essential lunge cards.
Dark Influences could be replaced by a couple of Direct Interventions
to cancel Entrancements and such. Two Garous and Ossian were stolen
from me during the finals...
2k9alastorsvilleins.name: Jacob's Pack

2k9alacrity1bc.author: Ira Fay
2k9alacrity1bc.description:
Description: Try to build up without looking like a huge threat, which
is tricky. Decrypt even while you have unique vampires in the
uncontrolled region, especially if you don't have Lumumba or all 4
clans yet. Cross-table oust if necessary to stablize the table. Use
the Abombwe's on 4-caps, so you can get them up to 5 for Ancestor
Spirit, or a bigger voter cap. Voter cap with Lumumba, since that's
the only vamp with PRE (if you get out 6 vamps, you have a ~76% chance
of getting Lumumba.)
2k9alacrity1bc.name: Team Africa

Cut through you like budur

2k9imperatorco.description: Title: The Ventrue Are Always Awesome
2k9imperatorco.name: Unknown

Torstensson. Martinelli's Ring was a metagame choice (it appeared I

the tournament).
2k9czestochowa.name: Guillaume Powerbleed

2k9falangoth.author: Alex Ek
2k9falangoth.description:

probably the weakest of the three. Something that makes people
underestimate the vampires you bring into play from time to time. The
deck is very versatile and features plenty of silver bullets which
helps you handle most situations you encounter.
2k9falangoth.name: Neo-Lawfirm

2k9psturku47.author: Ville Ruuskanen
2k9psturku47.description: Description: Really simple Tremere Anathema deck, no alchemy needed...
2k9psturku47.name: No Alchemy

2k9socnewark.description:
Title: Four Skills of Fury
Big Nos with Dominate also bring their usual bag of tricks to the party.
2k9socnewark.name: Unknown

2k9dmcun.author: Michael Heyder
2k9dmcun.description:
Description: 'Inspired' by a deck played by Erol Hammer at the German
Championship 2007. Nothing new or fancy. 'Wrong and Crosswise' was
huge, as was 'Kaymakli Fragment + Midget'. If your sitting next to a
Rush-Combat Deck, the game is over. Payload should be slightly
increased.
2k9dmcun.name: Demented Midgets

2k9crusademelbourne.author: Richard Aumann
2k9crusademelbourne.description:
Description: Speed is the game.. Require wormwood turn 2. Using
Afifa's special text to go forward with Gehenna cards and Anna's text
to placate opposition players. Nehemiah helps the library cycle cards
speed through the deck.
2k9crusademelbourne.name: Outrun the Worms 1.3

2k9bwhorth.author: Juan Oyarce
2k9bwhorth.event: Battle without honor or humanity - Tomoyasu Hotei
2k9bwhorth.name: Ventrue 2009 - ZERG v4

2k9karlsruhemq.author: Johannes Walch
2k9karlsruhemq.description:
Description: Basic idea was to use Command the Legion in any deck. I
made a G4/5 Ventrue, but was not too happy about it. Consulted the TWDA
and found Otto's G4/5 Ven, from where I borrowed a lot of ideas.

Crypt was nice, opted to double Johannes, well because it is
Johannes. Also I have Victor, never drew him, though. Most people have
DOM which is good.

Not too many surprises here. Monastery is cool, esp. when followed up
with a Parity Shift. I have 6 trifles there, master section is light
which is good because the deck cycles really fast.

Light on action cards since often your actions don't suceed, rather
have modifiers. Mind Rape are great doubling as defense and forward.
Command the Legion is really good when you can pull it off, disabling
blockers and deflecters and just Freak Drive afterwards.

Just enough payload to get the VPs. didnt have any seductions at
first, but this was very useful, just enough Freak Drives would have
missed every single one. Perfect Paragon is pretty good, versatility is
well worth the blood.

Light vote package to justify the Freak Drives and much needed
poolgain.

Just enough to keep people guessing

I was not sure at all about those cards, but both proved to be very
effective. Versatility really rules in this deck
2k9karlsruhemq.name: Johannes Commands the Legion

2k9mojlp.author: Teresa Neves
2k9mojlp.description:
Description: Classic design block denial bleed deck. From the times of
Luis Duarte up until today, little changed. Completely ignored combat.
Secret Passage, Secure Haven and a small cap can stop most of the
attacks. Promise of 1528 is awesome in post KoT environment.
2k9mojlp.name: Classic Giovanni Tap and Bleed

2k9kismarosmq.author: Martin Major
2k9kismarosmq.description: Description: Alastor based bruise and vote
2k9kismarosmq.name: Broken Brujahs

2k9mariettamq.description:
This is a minimally tweaked version of a Millenium Cultist Storyline Tournament Winning Deck.
One game win 3VP to get into finals, one game win 3vp in final.
2k9mariettamq.name: Law Firm says "Get off my lawn!" II

2k9wsnewark.author: James Messer
2k9wsnewark.name: Old School Anneke Aching Beauty Deck

2k9dtdgi.author: Enrico De Stefano
2k9dtdgi.description:
Description: This deck has been created around the Brujah Debate
card and designed to capitalize to the maximum the power of the
NEW CARTHAGE!!! Really a super-power card, especially in this
deck with lots of titled vampires of low capacity! Not so simply
to play but strong enough to resist in almost all situations!
2k9dtdgi.name: Rake's & Folker's Immortal Disarming SHOW !

2k9mwcharleston.author: Jeffrey Thompson
2k9mwcharleston.description:
1st round, sweep, 4VP
2nd round, tied, 2VP / 2vp with prey
Final round, won, 3VP with grand prey taking 2VP
2k9mwcharleston.name: I am I

2k9lvq.description:

and the Duals, bleed a bit, vote to kill.

2k9lvmq.description:

your prey.
2k9lvmq.name: Unknown

2k9bibuk.author: Hugh Angseesing
2k9bibuk.location: Stanhope Arms, Ashby Road, Burton upon Trent, England
2k9bibuk.name: I want to stick you with my third eye

2k9fhpri.author: Ben Peal
2k9fhpri.description:
Humo or Gemini crank out Nocturns and Underbridge Strays. Hannah
Montana and "We Like the Moon" Guedado get War Ghouls. Use Agent of
Power to bump up disciplines (especially for getting superior Strays)
or to give a Tzimisce Obtenebration for fast Nocturn + War Ghoul
action. Remember to use the presses from the Strays to help your War
Ghouls (I often used them to bail out of ANI combat). Deploy Corrupt

2k8fstilburg.author: Izaak Havelaar
2k8fstilburg.description:
This deck originally started as mono Auspex deck with guns and Black
Hand-tech for bloating purposes, but evolved into something that can
actually oust players as well. The gameplan is to feign being a bleed
deck that's not drawing into its payload while bloating enough to bring
out a few minions and equip one or two Magnums. Once you feel you're
pretty safe from your predator, start actively blocking your prey's
minions with Eagle's Sight and bleed hard into him. Once you have
secured a VP just bloat and block some more and be the last man
standing for the 3VP game win.

Taste of Vitae is vital to keep your bloat going and the Target Vitals
act a nasty surprise that deters combat decks from picking a fight with
you. It can also be used to knock out a weakened minion or put a rather
painful dent into a War Ghoul or some other ally. Other than that it's
really just a wall with a healthy amount of stealth bleed to go with it.

2k8originssun.author: Matthew Morgan
2k8originssun.description:
Description: The challenge I gave myself was to create a good
Daughters of Cacophony deck that wasn't a copy of
Ben Peal's NAC winning deck. This one is mostly
inspired by a deck of Forrest Nielsen's that won
a qualifier back in 2003 and made the NAC final the
same year. It adds !Toreador for bleed defense and
has a good chunk of combat defense. With another minute or two
left on the clock, I would've ousted my last prey for
a 3rd 4VP win (but I'm plenty satisfied with just a win).

Never saw Gael or Remilliard, who are probably the weakest crypt
choices here, so just as well. A couple other players have
insisted that this crypt needs Greta, but she wouldn't have
really helped this time. Sheila's +1 bleed and Fortitude were
just more useful.

Strangely, the Anarch Troublemakers never were that important
and I didn't draw them often. Could use another Pentex and
probably Direct Intervention. The Presence masters didn't
matter much since I mostly got out minions with PRE.

This seems like a lot, but I never discarded a bleed card and
often ran out. I probably had some chances to steal Hugh's
Carlton in the final, but he was really doing me more good
where he was, so I just bled with the Entrancements.

More Siren's Lure is a no-brainer, but this is all I own.
Oddly enough, most of my preys never tried to block me at
all, so again it didn't matter this time. Daring the Dawn
could certainly go here.

Only one Delaying Tactics? What was I thinking? It totally
saved me in round 1 and the final. Another copy should
certainly be here. Tourette's Voice was completely useless
and sadly misplayed a couple of times (sorry!). I thought it
might be good for saving grandpreys or for some unexpected
intercept, but the need never arose. Likewise, I think I
bounced one bleed in the entire tournament. That's something
you just can't plan for.

This worked out great. With all the other blood costs
in the deck, playing a Soak against hands for 1 is completely
worthwhile, which is mostly what I did with them.

2k8celestial2.author: Ira Fay
2k8celestial2.description:
Description: It's a little tricky to acquire 30 Trophy: Progeny irl
(thanks gNat and Ian!), but once you get them, this deck can be fun to
play. It reliably takes advantage of turns 1-3 master phases, which
are often wasted in most decks. Miller's special is incredibly good -
he is so perfect for this deck, and Anson compliments him
beautifully. My goal in designing this deck was to get a trophy deck
in the TWDA, and assuming I didn't make any stupid illegal deck
errors, I'm excited to post the first one. Trophy: Progeny is very
powerful in such large numbers, especially because it can act that
same turn. Choosing the right Red List target is tricky, because you
want something that you can burn, but other players can't. Whenever
possible, choose a target that your prey controls. Then, just sit
back and wait as long as possible, building the perfect combat hand,
holding the Palle Grande, playing 2-3 Trophies per turn. Try to
convince the table that you're not a threat (much easier when the
Palla Grande is in your hand, and not on the table.) If things are
flowing smoothly, you'll have 10+ Trophies on the table by turn ~8,
and then you can lunge when you're ready. If you have a fast
predator, bring up Anson first because he can Deflect, Parity Shift,
and 2nd Trad to keep you in the game. If you draw The Parthenon
early, you can consider bringing up Miller first. Without The
Parthenon, you'll hand jam on Masters. It's very rare that I discard
a Trophy: Progeny in this deck. Golconda was very helpful to keep me
(or an ally) in the game long enough for the combo to go off.

2k8nycqual.description:
Description: Get mummies. Block, fight, rush, bleed, win!

The larger vampires are obviously not meant to be influenced out and
never were. They might as well have been Enkidu, Hazimel, Sha-Ennu,
Saulot, etc., but it never really mattered as I rarely had a mummy
burned by losing all its life. Two copies of Halim and 3x Effective
Management meant I got him out in every preliminary round. In the
final he showed up late and ended up having to join the ranks of the
mummies.

The media outlets helped a lot. I'm a firm believer in Unmasking +
media locations in an ally deck. It really gets the job done.
Centralized Background Check was in my starting hand in the first two
games, but I didn't see it in round 3 when I was killed by .44s. Ah
well. It's good in theory.

Set's Curse was originally Far Mastery, but more of my crypt can play
Set's Curse and there are more available targets. In round 1, I was a
little slow with it and Meno Ngari got a skill card before I could hit
him with it. In round 2, I turned Lupo into a snake, which was really
cool, even if it probably didn't cause me to win any more than I was
already winning. I died too quickly to make use of it in round 3, but
turning one of Ben Peal's War Ghouls into a snake would've been pretty
great. There were small vampires that would've made good targets for
this in the final, but sadly I had nobody with SER to play it, so it
had to be discarded.

10x Spell of Life was pretty good in a 61 card deck. I normally got
the Spell off around turn 7 or so, I think. I never tried to get it to
happen again and never needed it. Each game concluded a turn or two
after I completed the Spell (or in the case of round 3, the game
concluded for me the turn before I would've completed it).

Heavy intercept would've probably been a problem for me, but luckily
there was none. My first prey of the day was an Akunanse deck, but I
managed to block it tooling up with intercept permanents. Veils were
good to add stealth to mummies (since I never had anyone with OBF for
cloak). Conditioning, just because I'd be crazy not to.

Carlton made frequent appearances. I had Ossian in round 2, but he
really only served to cycle my prey's Swallowed by the Night maneuvers.
I got Qetu out in the first round and actually successfully bled my
prey twice, which I think is pretty good (she bleeds for 2). An early
Nephren-Ka probably gave me the final, because I rushed the dom/obf
deck a lot to keep it from having the steam to oust me. I sadly never
had the pool to get Kherebutu or Tutu. I'll have to keep playing the
deck until I make good use of them. Vagabond Mystic was the 61st card
in this deck (originally designed at 60), but I never drew him.

I believe the only one of these I ever played was FBI Special Affairs
Division, which was really useful when Carlton was blocking Matata at 1
blood. Matata couldn't take the risk of going to torpor and never
coming back, so Carlton got away with dodging three or four times.
2k8nycqual.name: Mummy Strength!

2k8pwbsla2.author: Ira Fay

Description: Get a bunch of locations in play, a giant hand size, and
then win. Make sure Guillaume doesn't go to torpor. Ian loaned me

2k8ancestorspiritctsa.author: Daniel Boud
2k8ancestorspiritctsa.description:

is to get the tag-team combo of Venere and Klaus out, block key
actions, grab a .44 and hole up until the table plays out. Once other
decks start losing their legs begin turning the screws with a few big
bleeds (Palla Grande/Aire of Elation), playing a Smiling Jack and
dropping a strategic Pentex Subversion. The lower cap vamps are there
purely for weenie support; playing the odd Art Scam and for the Palla
Grande bleed push. As always, I over did the master card count. ;)

2k8fotekpsa.description:
This was our national constructed tournament event held at Upcon 2008.
There was a good attendence at this tournament and the metagame was
dominated by bruise-bleed decks. The final table was swept up by Victor,
after some cunning tabletalk and strategic deal-breaking.

The final table looked like this:
Victor playing Sneak/Bleed Protean Dominate bleeding
Jacque playing Kiasyd Sneak/Bleed toolbox bleeding
Michael playing Tupdog and Friends rush deck bleeding
Jesse playing Setite are tempting and enticing deck bleeding

2k8mexicoqualifier.author: Matthew Morgan
2k8mexicoqualifier.description:
Description: I suppose there's not a ton of strategy here except that
it's better to bleed for a lot with everyone than bleed for a lot with
only one or two minions.

Maybe 2 more Stone Travel and a couple Shroud of Absence would be good
here since Quincy and Dame Hollerton can't get stealth from the other
Mytherceria cards. My Shrouds were in another deck when I built this
one and I didn't have them with me when I decided to play this one.

Combat was practically irrelevant to this tournament. I could've
dropped all these cards. Never played the Entombment. It's mostly
only there for allies since most of my crypt only has obt.

I had high hopes for Blind Spot, but it was never useful. It would be
better to have a Jake Washington or two or maybe a Prophecies of
Gehenna. In fact, I tried to borrow one of those before the
tournament, but none were to be found.

Much better than Vessel in this deck. All those Dominate cards bleed
my vampires dry. Can't afford to delay gratification with Vessels.

Those Mexicans beat me to the punch in all four rounds!

See? No need for Vessel. I Suddened my predator's Vessel in the final
to keep a Blood Doll on Quincy.

A couple Delaying Tactics or even Covencraft wouldn't be a terrible
idea here.
2k8mexicoqualifier.name: La Cancion de la Patata Magica

2k8TempleConcordance.author: Matthew Morgan
2k8TempleConcordance.description:
Description: Continuing in my quest to with a tournament with
every clan alphabetically, I had to put together an Ahrimanes
deck. I hadn't ever played them much and generally felt like
they were a decent clan, but Howler always goes to torpor, so
that's a pretty major liability. I asked for some advice on
the #vtes irc chat and eventually jhattara gave me the idea of
playing your traditional blocking felines with some Anarch Revolts
to speed the table up. Great idea! Still not having much experience
with Ahrmanes, I basically copied David Quinonero's famous deck
and shoehorned some Anarch Revolts. It turned out pretty well,
if a little slow. I won my first round by the skin of my teeth
and had to settle for a 2-2 split in the 2nd as my prey sort of
ran away with the table. The deck was ideal for the more
deliberately-played final and I won with 2.5VP.

I decided to throw a couple small guys in, but in general
they weren't super helpful. The deck is basically Howler
with maybe The Siamese or Cynthia filling in if Howler is
unwilling or unable to perform her duties.

Not free and doesn't provide a press. Can we get some
errata? The one time I tried to play this it was Suddened.

The Anarch Revolts and Fame were responsible for both my
game wins. I think I nailed a couple Blood Dolls with Vessels,
but I mostly included them over Blood Dolls because I was
worried about master hand jam.

Didn't need Aranthebes because of a lack of weenie predators.
I mostly played the Enchant Kindreds at inferior, so they might've
been better bleed cards (Legal, Social, Entrancement?). 4x Nose
of the Hound was pretty nice.

Okay, so I actually got my firsts ousts in the games I
won by bleeding for 2 at 1 stealth, but I like to think the
Anarch Revolts and Fame are what got me there. These were
pretty good for keeping things up close and personal with
Flash Harrison.

Never when I needed it. Sigh. Same with the Guardian Angel.

This was mostly only good for backousting Jesse when he
wouldn't let Howler out of a Pentex.

I nearly lost the first game because I just couldn't draw
any untap or intercept and my prey was getting away with murder
for it. It's weird because this looks like plenty to me.

The Murders are pretty good here in that they make up for
the fact that the support crew have inferior Animalism (not
too scary on its own) and let Howler save on blood by doing
a good amount of damage from long range.

Pretty light combat package, especially since 8 of those
cards don't actually do anything to hurt the opponent or
protect my minion. The deck obviously relies heavily on
Howler's natural abilities and whatever permanents it can
put together. Some Leapfrog or Majesty or something might've
been good, but I didn't feel like there was room for it
and it was more important to be able to hurt opposing minions.
2k8TempleConcordance.name: Howling Anarchs

2k8tfnwesterville.author: Matt Piatek
2k8tfnwesterville.description:
Description: Demdemeh makes a herd of elephant allies with 2 hand
damage and one bleed. Babalawo Alafin combines with Maabara to allow
you to craft the hand you need.

It didn't work the way it was intended to in the finals. In retrospect
I should have brought out Demdemeh instead of Wamukota as my second
vampire, but I thought his ability would be important for my retain
actions(it was never used). I never could get enough pool to bring
out Demdemeh afterwards. A herd of elephants would have greatly
increased my ousting ability.

It is nice to know that the deck can survive without all of the "A"
team in play.
2k8tfnwesterville.name: Tembo!!

2k8jmisantiago.author: Hernán Rodríguez
2k8jmisantiago.description: Description: If you don't have votes, just bleed.
2k8jmisantiago.name: Lasombra vote bleed

2k8psbilbao.author: Iñaki Jiménez Alonso
2k8psbilbao.description:
Description: This is the second tournament win with the deck. Should
include 2-3 vessels but everything else seems to work really well. The
only real problem comes if the prey is straight forward as he can go
with 3VP befor you can even try to stop him. I stole the final from
my malk B&S prey with his own major boon thanks to the fragment
playing it on my predator to keep him alive just enough time for the
GW
2k8psbilbao.name: Gangrel Wall

2k8longmontbenediction.author: Darby Keeney
2k8longmontbenediction.description:
Description: [CEL] gun

Built so that I could better understand the way [CEL] gun decks win
tables. Named in honor of my friend Kevin's critique of the 1st cut
deck design at the 2006 NAC.

I pay slightly more than the bare minimum for G1/2 vampires with
[CEL] to support Atonement and a touch of [pre].

One Waste Management Operations could fit in here.

It's rare to feel that I need more rushes to impact both predator and prey.
I think this is the right number, combined with the 3 Frontal Assaults.

Never seen impactful use - this would be my first cull.

The combat package is pretty bulky - but is resilient and pretty effective

I seldom count on equip actions for the .44, so the NRA PAC should be culled.

The 3-card vote package is the most consistent source of pool damage in this deck,
despite my vampires' lack of titles.

These should probably be "Eluding the Arms of Morpheus" for Yawp Court and Atonement.
2k8longmontbenediction.name: Mergen's Quandry

2k8fillipberkeley.author: Ira Fay
2k8fillipberkeley.description:
Description: Get a giant hand size and win. It's fun! Cards I
intended to include but couldn't find before the tournament: Benedict
Giovanni, Esoara, Almodo Giovanni, and Earl in my crypt, and
Filchware's, Club Zombie, PB: Cape Verde, Parthenon, Brothers Grimm,
and Palatial Estate in my Library. At the tournament, I played
against Esoara, Earl, and Parthenon, so I'm glad I didn't end up
contesting them!
2k8fillipberkeley.name: Gio hand size bruise/bleed

2k8momom.author: John Eno
2k8momom.description:
Midget would be much better as The Colonel or Evan Klein. I discarded
the hunting ground during every game in which I saw it. I drew Kite
in every game, and his bonus intercept was so effective that I'd consider
adding a second copy, or a copy of Anatole. (Actually, given how much
I ended up paying for Midget in most of the games today, he might be
usefully replaced by either of them.)
2k8momom.name: Prostitute Laundry

2k8capetownswarm.author: Adrianna Pinska
2k8capetownswarm.description:
Description: The deck is fairly straight-forward. Take over your
prey's minions to bleed themselves out. Keep Saulot and your pool
going with Renewed Vigors. On hindsight, the Heidelberg's were more
useful than the use they were intended for (transferring blood from
Renewed Vigors).
2k8capetownswarm.name: Saulot the Puppeteer

2k7togphelsinki.author: Teemu Sainomaa
2k7togphelsinki.description:
Description: I thought now that we have better prices and high cost
for the tournament, there would be more S/B decks. Pool gain was good
with locations and vessels.

should add 1 more, don't know what to take out

was great threat against daring the dawn with procurer:
2k7togphelsinki.name: Power of Auspex

2k7campeonatojuizforano.author: Pedro Paulo de Sousa Mendes
2k7campeonatojuizforano.description:
Description: The deck's goal is to setup as fast as you can by
depleting your library and to use Unity/Anthelios to cycle back
whatever master you need the most at the time.

It was enough. I never needed more than this.

Heart is no good when it shows up late, but this is a small price
to pay when compared to how good it is when I draw it early (it was
decisive in the final table).

I only packed the extremely necessary events, so I wouldn't draw
any extra table hate, and was lucky enough to put all 3 in play in
every game. The decks runs wonderfully with those 3 on the table.
2k7campeonatojuizforano.name: Imbued at Last

2k7nsftmmallorca.author: Ginés Quiñonero
2k7nsftmmallorca.description:
Description: Bring out the highest capacity vampire in your uncontrolled
region. Once he or she is in play, play Danse Macabre on him/her and have
him/her perform two actions per turn (The Call & bleed, most of the time,
or Revelations & bleed, etc.). Thus, you should be able to put a few
vampires in play at a low cost and quickly. The rest is easy: bleed your
preys to death:)
2k7nsftmmallorca.event: No Secrets from the Magaji: Marratxí
2k7nsftmmallorca.name: Mad Dancers

2k7avazaragoza.author: Miguel del Valle
2k7avazaragoza.name: Me pareció ver un lindo gatito

2k7mbsatl0.author: John Newquist
2k7mbsatl0.description:
Daneel is correct - if a card is weak, I should stop playing it.
There should be one additional Flash Grenade in the deck - it's
entirely possible someone else from the event has it.
2k7mbsatl0.name: Champion is Weak

2k7fsmc.author: Omael Rangel
2k7fsmc.description:
4 Memories of Mortality -- when they are gone i should add a fort. library, a Pentex Subversion and maybe Anarch Troublemaker
6 Computer Hacking -- maybe add 1 more
3 Glancing Blows -- I'll remove this and add more Concealed and Molotovs
1 .44 Magnum -- this should be another Grenade but i only had 7 at the time
2k7fsmc.name: Nephandi

2k7mbscolumbus.author: James Messer
2k7mbscolumbus.description:
Description: James won all four of his rounds with
skilled play, smooth table talk, deal breaking,
and this deck:

PS: The Church of the Order of St. Blaise has no effect in this deck.
It was mistakenly included with the idea of creating a permanent Palla Grande.
2k7mbscolumbus.name: Unknown

2k7fsboston.description: Description: Get out lots of Lasombra and win.
2k7fsboston.name: Army of Shadows
